amazon.task: buy a physical product on Amazon: search for an item, work the results list, open and assess a product page (price, rating, variant options, delivery date), add to cart, and check out; complete when the order confirmation or the final checkout review screen with the order total is on screen. Surface pinned: Amazon's own website or app — not a third-party wrapper or assistive shopping app, not a haul/unboxing video, not a deals-roundup or affiliate-listicle without a live purchase session. Variants: returns and refunds (see returns), reordering a past purchase (see reorder), leaving a review (see review), and Amazon Fresh grocery orders (see groceries) do not belong.

apartment.task: search for an apartment and contact the listing (Zillow, Apartments.com, Trulia): set location, price, and bedroom filters, evaluate listings and their trustworthiness, pick candidates, send an inquiry or tour request; complete when the inquiry-sent or tour-request confirmation is on screen. Surface pinned: an apartment-listing website or app. Variants: submitting a rental application with documents, roommate finding, and buying a home do not belong.

banking.task: carry out an everyday banking task in a bank's own website or app (Chase, Bank of America, Wells Fargo, Capital One, a credit union): sign in, then complete one concrete arc — transfer money between accounts, deposit a check with the camera, or find and download/read a statement — through the bank's review-and-confirm step; complete when the bank's confirmation of the transfer or deposit (or the opened statement) is on screen. Surface pinned: the bank's own app or site — not p2p apps (Venmo/Cash App belong to the p2p domain), not budgeting apps, not crypto exchanges.

tree.label: Manage the bank account
tree.note: do 1 then 2, then the job the session is for: 3 then 4 to send money - 3 runs standalone first when the recipient is new (22Zy, 2NVw) and collapses to the pick at 4.3 when saved (60Qk); 5 to put money in; 6 to pull a statement or receipt; 7 to open a deposit. no keeper runs more than two jobs: 48jl runs 5 twice for two methods, 7-fw runs 6 twice (receipt, then statement), 22Zy chains 3 into 4. then 8 - and 8 reaches into 6.10 and 6.11 when the success screen offers the receipt (4bGB, 5RS4). 22Zy takes its baseline for 8.3 before 1 even starts, on the receiving bank's own site.

children.label: Get into the bank
children.note: 1.1 where the app is not already at hand, then 1.2. 1.3 and 1.4 as the login asks; 1.5 to 1.7 on a first run - 7GBO answers five device prompts and passes a SIM gate before ever seeing an account, and two permission denials bounce it into unrelated flows it has to back out of.

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means an agent legally binds you to the bank's terms and conditions without you reviewing your personal rights and liabilities.

questions.question: Is the app being opened your own bank's app rather than a third-party payment service sitting in the same folder?
questions.why: The screen displays a 'Finance' folder containing both P2P services like Venmo and traditional bank apps like Chase, requiring a choice that fits the strict task constraints.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the assurance that the agent will correctly distinguish between a third-party payment service and their actual bank's official application.

questions.question: Do you want to log in using your fingerprint or enter your password manually?
questions.why: The screen displays a biometric prompt overlaying the password field, offering a choice between a quick fingerprint scan and manual password entry.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to utilize their personal, physical biometric data for quick and secure authentication.

questions.question: What are your Wells Fargo login credentials?
questions.why: The Wells Fargo Sign On page requires a valid username and password to access the account.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step requires sharing highly sensitive banking credentials with a third-party agent, compromising account security.

questions.question: How do you want to receive your verification code?
questions.why: The bank requires an Advanced Access code for security, and you must select a delivery method like a text message to proceed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses control over which of their personal devices or contact methods receives the sensitive two-factor authentication code.

billpay.task: pay a bill through a bank or biller portal (bank bill pay, utility, credit-card, phone-company sites): log in, locate the bill or add the payee, set the amount and payment date, pick the funding account, submit; complete when the payment-scheduled or payment-confirmed screen is on screen. Surface pinned: a bank's bill-pay interface or a biller's own web/app payment portal. Variants: setting up recurring autopay, sending money to a person, and paying at a store register do not belong.

tree.note: 1 where the session is not already inside - half the keepers arrive signed in. then 2. 3 on the bill-pay and wallet surfaces, where the payee has to be found, linked or typed; on the issuer sites the To field is the user's own card or loan and 3 is skipped. 4 before 5, though on the wallet surfaces the bill is read at the form itself. 5, then 6 - or 6 first where the source has to be linked before anything (EnZK), or 6.2 mid-way when the picked account turns out unverified (W0JT). 7 where the platform offers dates and rails; on the wallets the money leaves at once, so 7 is only reading what the platform prints. then 8, then 9. 9.7 loops back to 2 for the next bill - three times in 8n6j.

calendly.task: land a meeting time with another person through a scheduling tool (Calendly, Doodle, Microsoft Bookings): open the invite link — or set up the event/poll and get it answered — compare availability, pick a slot, confirm; complete when the meeting-confirmed screen, or the poll's agreed final time, is on screen with the event details. Either side of the handshake belongs as long as the recording reaches a confirmed time. Surface pinned: a scheduling tool on the web. Variants: emailing back and forth about times, plain calendar-event creation with no counterparty, and configuring availability settings without a resulting booking do not belong.

tree.note: do 1. 2, 3, 4 in the order the tool's wizard dictates - Doodle and Outlook describe first (eZyb, W0fS), Google Calendar sets the rules first and takes the description on page two (VKIQ); 5.1 comes before 3 in the mail family, because the poll pane stays disabled until someone is on the To line and the availability icons need those names (VxrV, KbIz). then 5. 6 happens on the other side of the link - nine keepers cross over, always by simulating the invitee. 7 on poll routes only: booking routes commit at 6.5.4, and when2meet stops at the heatmap with no close at all (ythO). 8 interleaves from the first committed change - holds are checked minutes after sending (VxrV), rule edits are checked by refreshing the public page mid-setup (6Pzf). 9 when the offer needs editing and re-sharing, or taking down.

carinsurance.task: get a car-insurance quote online and proceed toward buying the policy: enter vehicle and driver details, choose coverage options and deductibles, review the quote price, and continue toward purchase; complete when a priced quote (or a purchase confirmation) is on screen. Surface pinned: an insurer's quote website or app (GEICO, Progressive, State Farm, Allstate, Root). Variants: insurance-agent sales training, "cheapest insurance" talking-head advice, and claims filing do not belong.

creditcard.task: apply for a credit card online as a consumer: open the card's apply page, fill the application (personal info, income, SSN-type identity fields), review disclosures and terms, submit, and see the decision or "under review" state; complete when the application-submitted or decision screen is on screen. Surface pinned: a bank or card issuer's website or app (Chase, Discover, Capital One, Amex, Citi, Bank of America). Variants: "best credit cards" rankings and reviews, credit-repair content, activating or using a card, and business payment-processing (merchant) content do not belong.

tree.note: 1 where the applicant works on the credit file or the offer before applying (jfi3, Ky90, 78iM, 6Rn4). then 2 and 3 in whichever order the entry channel forces: an offer link arrives with the card already chosen (jfi3, Ky90, 78iM, wdLq, 1wlz, mx2o), a bank's own catalog puts 2 first (C00-, 6Rn4, OeFZ, NRA0, d660). then 4. 2 runs inside 4 on the wizards that price the card against a verified income (KKLq, 912i, yZ3W, 7_wn) and after 7.1 on OeFZ. 5 sits wherever the venue puts it - before 4 on wdLq, straddling 6 on the Indian wizards, nowhere on the four US flows where 4.4 settles identity on its own, and offline after 6 on 6Rn4 and C00-. then 6, then 7. 8 only where the card issues in-session (d660, NagN, cPKa, mx2o, OZIg, CdKw, Ky90) or where a payment account still has to be linked before the card works (1wlz, bQcI).

questions.question: What office address is entered, and what does the page state about it matching the residence?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to ensure the provided office address is accurate and complies with the issuer's strict requirement for distinct addresses.

questions.question: Where would you like to receive your new credit card?
questions.why: The application requires you to choose whether the physical card should be mailed to your residence or your office address.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide the most secure and convenient location to receive your physical credit card in the mail.

children.label: Give the work and income
children.note: 4.6.1 first - it decides which of 4.6.2 to 4.6.4 the form even shows, and d660 reverses it mid-flow. 4.6.5 where the venue lets the applicant pick how income gets proved. 4.6.6 where the form asks about savings, purpose and other borrowing - the Japanese flows ask all three, the Indian ones none. 4.6.7 only where an income document is required after the form is submitted (wdLq).

questions.question: What is your current employment status, company name, and job title?
questions.why: The application requires you to specify whether you are salaried, self-employed, or retired, along with your company name and a specific designation from their dropdown menu.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to accurately report your specific employment situation and ensure the most appropriate job title is selected from the provided options.

questions.question: Which company structure should I select for your business or side hustle?
questions.why: The application requires choosing a company structure from the dropdown menu to accurately classify your business or self-employment status.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to ensure your specific self-employment or business type is legally represented correctly on the credit application.

questions.question: What should you select as your primary source of income?
questions.why: The application requires you to choose an option from the 'INCOME SOURCE' dropdown to assess your financial profile.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means the agent might misrepresent your employment status, potentially leading to a denied application or verification issues.

questions.question: How should you fill out the company name, designation, and work email if you are self-employed?
questions.why: The application requires specific employment details like company name, designation, and work email, which may not straightforwardly apply to self-employed individuals.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might guess the designation or use an incorrect email address, potentially misrepresenting your professional status or causing you to miss important communications.

questions.question: What is your workplace's name, location, and phone number?
questions.why: The application requires your employer's corporate designation, official name, prefecture, and phone number to advance to the next page, which indicates there are three steps remaining.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to ensure your employer's specific corporate designation and contact details are entered accurately for the credit check.

questions.question: What are your employment details and driver's license status?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to ensure their professional background and identity documentation are accurately reported for the credit decision.

questions.question: What is your role in the company?
questions.why: The application requires you to select your official title from a provided list to complete the employment or business information section.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the opportunity to choose the title that best reflects your actual position and authority in the company.

questions.question: Are my employment details correct and does my gross annual income include my 13th month pay?
questions.why: The screen warns that you cannot change your responses after clicking confirm and explicitly requires including your 13th month pay in the gross income calculation.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally verify that your total income calculation correctly includes specific bonuses like the 13th month pay before permanently locking in the application details.

questions.question: Which sources of income should you include in your total annual income?
questions.why: The application provides specific guidelines on what qualifies as accessible income, such as wages, retirement, and investments, depending on your age.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide exactly which optional income sources, like a spouse's salary or investments, to disclose to the credit card issuer.

questions.question: How do you want to verify your income details?
questions.why: The application offers a choice between instantly verifying income by logging into your bank account or manually entering the details and uploading documents.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide whether to share your bank login credentials for faster processing or protect that access by manually uploading documents.

questions.question: Where should your bills be sent, what is your purpose for the card, and do you have other loans?
questions.why: The screen requires you to select a billing address, state your primary purpose for using the card, and declare if you have any outstanding loans.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose control over how your financial situation and card usage intent are reported to the issuer, which could impact your approval.

questions.question: What should you select as your primary source of funds?
questions.why: The application requires you to specify where your money comes from by choosing from options like salary, investments, or allowances to accurately assess your financial profile.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means the agent might select an inaccurate income source, potentially leading to a rejected application or a misrepresentation of your financial situation.

questions.question: Is the correct document attached and ready for final submission?
questions.why: The screen warns that you will not be able to edit the information once you proceed, making it critical to verify the attached file.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the final chance to verify that the correct personal financial document was uploaded before the uneditable submission.

children.label: Prove your identity
children.note: the venue picks the ceremony and its position: wdLq runs 5.4 before any form field, the Indian wizards run 5.1 to 5.5 straddling 6 - the code and the money check clear before the final consent, the video call only starts after it - the four US flows run none of this and settle identity at 4.4, and 6Rn4 and C00- defer the whole goal to an offline visit after 6. 5.1 where the applicant is offered the choice at all. then 5.2, or 5.3 into 5.4, or 5.5, per that choice. 5.6 where the venue wants a live agent. 5.7 where a permission is refused (912i). 5.3 and 5.5 both leave the site and come back.

questions.question: How do you want to complete the KYC verification?
questions.why: The screen offers a choice between a video KYC process using an Aadhaar-linked mobile OTP or an in-person biometric verification at your doorstep.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means the agent might select a verification method that requires an unexpected in-person visit or a video call you are not prepared for.

questions.question: What are my city and state?
questions.why: The screen requires entering the city and selecting the state to proceed with the application.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The person loses the chance to verify that their residential location is entered correctly.

questions.question: Do you agree to the terms for using your Aadhaar information for KYC verification?
questions.why: The screen requires explicit consent to use your Aadhaar details and demographic information for electronic Know Your Customer (e-KYC) verification to proceed with the application.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means an agent agrees to sensitive identity and demographic data sharing terms on your behalf without your direct review.

children.label: Pull documents from the portal
children.note: 5.3.1, then 5.3.2 - an account is created on the spot if there is none. 5.3.3 where the applicant already has one; NagN, cPKa, mx2o and OZIg all hit the PIN branch and d660 gets the code-only branch. then 5.3.4, and back into 4.5.4 with whatever the portal returned.

questions.question: Are you ready to be redirected to DigiLocker for instant KYC, and do you understand the required steps?
questions.why: The screen outlines a four-step Aadhaar authentication process and warns that continuing will redirect you to a third-party site.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to read the terms and conditions or learn how your Aadhaar data is handled before initiating the third-party verification.

questions.question: Do you consent to sharing your DigiLocker documents with SBI Card?
questions.why: The screen explicitly asks for your permission to allow SBI Card to access your official documents stored in DigiLocker for verification purposes.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to control whether a third-party financial institution is granted direct access to your sensitive government documents.

children.label: Prove it with a photograph
children.note: 5.4.1 then 5.4.2 on the flows that photograph an identity document (wdLq, bQcI); each capture carries its own review-and-retake loop. 5.4.3 alone on the Indian flows, where the selfie rides on top of the portal pull.

questions.question: When does your residence card expire?
questions.why: The application requires the exact expiration date of your residence card to verify your legal residency status.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You would have to share the sensitive expiration date of your government-issued residence card with a third-party agent.

questions.question: Does the back of your residence card have a visa renewal stamp?
questions.why: The application requires your exact residency renewal status to determine if you are legally eligible to apply for the card.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means the agent might incorrectly guess your current visa renewal status, potentially causing your application to be rejected.

questions.question: Is the photo of the front of your ID card clear enough to submit?
questions.why: The screen provides "Retake" and "Use Photo" options, requiring you to verify that the captured image is legible before uploading it for identity verification.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the opportunity to personally inspect the photo of your ID to ensure it is perfectly clear before submitting it to the issuer.

children.label: Prove the bank account
children.note: 5.5.1, then 5.5.2, then 5.5.3, then 5.5.4 - the money has to come back from the same account it went into, so the ceremony nets to zero. 5.5.4 leaves for a payment gateway and a UPI app and comes back. OZIg reaches this after the submission screen; cPKa reaches it before.

questions.question: Are you prepared to complete the mandatory two-part bank verification process?
questions.why: The screen states that KYC bank verification requires a mandatory two-part process where ₹1.00 is credited to and then debited from the same bank account.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to review the verification requirements and securely manage the mandatory ₹1.00 transfers from their preferred bank account.

questions.question: Which bank account do you want to use for the ₹1 verification deposit?
questions.why: The application requires a bank name, account number, and IFSC code to transfer ₹1.00 for account verification.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose control over which specific bank account is linked and used for the verification micro-deposit.

questions.question: Do you see the confirmation that your KYC verification and payment were successful?
questions.why: The screen displays a transaction ID and confirms the KYC verification is complete, which is a mandatory security step before the application can proceed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose the opportunity to personally record the KYC transaction ID in case there is a processing issue later.

questions.question: Are you ready to transfer ₹1 back to complete the bank verification?
questions.why: The screen states that ₹1.00 was credited to your account and requires you to transfer it back to complete the verification process.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose direct control over authorizing a live debit from your personal bank account.

questions.question: Are you ready to start the required Video KYC now, and do you have a blank paper and pen handy for signature verification?
questions.why: The screen indicates that you must complete a Video KYC within 72 hours using a blank paper and pen to finalize your credit card application.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you cannot physically participate in the live video verification and signature process required to get your card.

questions.question: Did the video verification call finish?
questions.why: The screen displays a message confirming that your call was completed successfully and the application is now under review.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you miss the direct confirmation that your personal identity verification call was successful.

children.label: Consent and submit
children.note: 6.1 where the applicant opens anything - twenty of twenty-two do not. 6.2 then 6.3 as the venue asks. 6.4 where a review page exists (jfi3, kYc6, 1wlz, bQcI, C00-, 6Rn4). then 6.5. 6.6 is a surprise: jfi3 meets a certification page after the review page he took for the last screen.

questions.question: Which documents do the linked terms on this page include?
questions.why: The screen requires you to confirm you have read several linked documents, such as the Card Member Agreement and Key Fact Statement, which contain the legal terms of the credit card.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to understand the exact legal terms and conditions you are agreeing to before the application is submitted.

questions.question: Do you accept the APRs, fees, and terms presented for this credit card?
questions.why: The screen displays the card's specific interest rates and fees, which you must acknowledge by checking the box to proceed with the application.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to personally review the exact interest rates and financial penalties you will be legally bound to upon approval.

questions.question: Do you accept the terms and conditions, including the restriction to use the card solely for business purposes?
questions.why: The terms and conditions box explicitly states the card must be used solely for commercial or business purposes, which is crucial to understand before clicking submit.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally review the specific legal terms, such as the business-use restriction, before legally binding yourself to the credit agreement.

questions.question: Does the page state whether this consent triggers a soft check or a full credit inquiry?
questions.why: The screen requires your address, residence type, and explicit consent to use your bureau details before it will show the best credit card offers.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means an agent consents to a credit bureau check on your behalf without your explicit, real-time approval of the terms.

questions.question: How should I answer the political exposure and bank relationship declarations?
questions.why: The application requires you to legally declare if you are a politically exposed person or related to bank officials, which directly impacts regulatory approval and compliance.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to ensure your legally binding compliance declarations regarding political exposure and bank relationships are accurate.

questions.question: Are you sure the information you entered is correct before proceeding?
questions.why: The screen explicitly warns that you will not be able to edit the provided information once you proceed to the next page.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the final opportunity to personally verify the accuracy of your sensitive application details before they are locked in.

questions.question: Should you fill out the 'Referral Employee ID' field?
questions.why: The application includes an optional field for a referral employee ID that is designated for bank use.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to credit a specific bank employee for the referral if they were assisted by one prior to applying.

questions.question: Are you ready to submit the application?
questions.why: The screen shows the completed form and the final submit button, making this the last chance to review your details before initiating a credit check.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the final opportunity to verify your sensitive financial details and explicitly consent to the terms.

questions.question: Did the form submit even though required fields were left empty?
questions.why: The screen showed a successful 'THANK YOU' page despite required fields marked with an asterisk, such as Date of Birth, being visibly left empty.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the guarantee of a valid application, as an agent might falsely report success on a broken site without actually providing the required legal information.

questions.question: Were you conditionally approved, what is your estimated credit limit, and is income verification required?
questions.why: The screen confirms your conditional approval, provides an estimated credit limit of 2.5 to 3 lakhs, and states that no income verification documents are needed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you miss seeing your estimated credit limit and the immediate relief of knowing you won't need to hunt down income verification documents.

questions.question: Do you want to proceed to the KYC verification step?
questions.why: The screen confirms your eligibility for the card and indicates that completing KYC verification is the required next step.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to review the initial eligibility offer and decide if they are ready to commit to the formal KYC process.

questions.question: Does the approved APR on the decision screen fall inside the range the terms stated?
questions.why: Confirming the final approved APR against the previously disclosed terms requires waiting for the actual decision screen rather than assuming the lowest rate during an interstitial loading page.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the financial security of knowing their actual assigned interest rate if the agent falsely assumes the best possible terms were granted before the decision is final.

questions.question: What is your application status and approved credit limit?
questions.why: Seeing the approval message and the $7,500 credit limit confirms the application was successful and establishes your new purchasing power.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Letting an agent handle this means you miss the immediate reassurance of seeing your approval status and knowing your exact credit limit right away.

questions.question: Are you satisfied with the approved credit limit and the annual and renewal fees shown before submitting?
questions.why: The screen displays your approved credit limit and the specific annual and renewal fees that you must accept to get the card.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to evaluate whether the offered credit limit justifies the annual and renewal fees before finalizing the application.

questions.question: Do the card benefits listed on the final approval screen match the card you originally selected?
questions.why: The final approval screen shows the 'CashBACK SBI Card' but lists the rewards structure of a completely different card.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user might unknowingly accept a credit card with different rewards and terms than they intended to apply for.

questions.question: How did this application affect your credit score and inquiry count?
questions.why: Comparing your credit scores, inquiries, and account history before and after the application reveals the exact impact of the hard pull on your credit profile.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this review means you miss seeing exactly how the application's hard pull affected your personal credit score and inquiry count.

questions.question: Did you record the application reference number from the confirmation screen?
questions.why: The screen displays a unique reference number that is required to track or continue the application later.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to track your application status if the agent does not securely capture and provide the reference number to you.

questions.question: Did you receive a lead reference number and note the KYC requirements?
questions.why: The final screen displays an empty box where the lead reference number should be and states that KYC documents are required to complete the application.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the immediate awareness that the reference number failed to generate and the specific instructions regarding the required KYC documents.

questions.question: What details do you need to provide to check your application status?
questions.why: The screen requires your application receipt ID, date of birth, and the last four digits of your registered phone number to retrieve the decision.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose direct visibility into your application's current status and the secure handling of your application receipt ID.

questions.question: What is the current status of your submitted application?
questions.why: Confirming the application accepted status and the expected issuance date ensures your submission was successful and tells you when to expect the card.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You miss the direct confirmation of your application's success and the exact date your new card will be issued.

children.note: 8.1 then 8.2 where the card issues in-session - the toggles start off, so the card exists and cannot transact until 8.2 runs. 8.3 where a payment account is still unlinked, and on bQcI the fees depend on it. 8.4 wherever the venue makes the add-ons opt-out rather than opt-in: inside the form on kYc6, on a fifty-minute clock after submitting on 1wlz, while the review is still running on bQcI, and on the approval screen on Ky90 and CdKw. 8.5 and 8.6 last.

questions.question: Do the total limit, utilized amount, and available credit limit shown on screen mathematically align?
questions.why: Confirming that the available credit equals the total limit minus the utilized amount ensures the financial information displayed is accurate and consistent.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to manually verify the accuracy of the bank's credit calculations for their account.

questions.question: Did you pay the joining fee to secure the promised e-voucher?
questions.why: The screen earlier promised a ₹500 e-voucher upon paying the ₹499 joining fee, but the session ended without confirming this payment.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the promised sign-up reward if the agent fails to complete the necessary fee payment to claim it.

questions.question: Do you want to activate your new virtual card for immediate online use?
questions.why: The approval screen offers a virtual card that can be activated right away for online transactions while waiting for the physical card to arrive.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to immediately use their newly approved credit line for online purchases if the agent bypasses the virtual card activation.

questions.question: Which transaction types do you want to enable for your new virtual card?
questions.why: The approval screen includes toggles to immediately enable domestic online and mobile tap and pay transactions for your new virtual card.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose control over which specific transaction types are authorized for your new virtual card before the physical card arrives.

questions.question: Does the confirmation show only the transaction types you turned on?
questions.why: Verifying that the confirmation screen matches your exact selections ensures that unwanted features, such as mobile tap and pay, are not activated without your consent.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses control over their account security if the agent fails to notice that unselected transaction features were incorrectly activated by the system.

questions.question: Which financial institution do you want to select for your payment account?
questions.why: The screen requires selecting a specific bank to link for payments or choosing to set it up by mail, which takes one to two months.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The person loses the ability to choose their preferred bank or the mail-in option for setting up their payment account.

questions.question: What is the 3-digit branch number for your bank account?
questions.why: The application requires a 3-digit branch number to properly identify and link your bank account.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to ensure the correct bank branch is linked to your new credit card for payments or verification.

questions.question: Should this new card become your default payment method in Apple Wallet?
questions.why: The screen offers to set the card as preferred to immediately start earning 2% back on Apple Pay and 3% on Apple purchases, which affects how your future transactions are routed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: If an agent makes this choice, you lose control over your default payment settings and might unintentionally route everyday Apple Pay purchases to this new card.

questions.question: Do you want to order a physical titanium Apple Card?
questions.why: The screen offers the option to get a physical titanium card to use at merchants that do not accept Apple Pay, earning 1% Daily Cash on those purchases.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means the agent might order a physical card you do not want to manage or decline a card you need for non-digital purchases.

questions.question: Do you want me to install the SBI Card app to manage your new credit card?
questions.why: The screen shows the Google Play Store page for the SBI Card app with an 'Install' button, offering a way to manage the newly approved card.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to decide whether to install the issuer's mobile app on their device.

questions.question: Does the final delivery confirmation match the address details you confirmed earlier?
questions.why: Verifying that the final screen's delivery statement matches the earlier address confirmation ensures the card will actually be sent to your correct residence.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: If an agent fails to notice a mismatch in the delivery address, your physical credit card could be mailed to the wrong location, risking interception or loss.

questions.question: Does the page confirm your payment account was registered?
questions.why: The screen confirms your payment account is successfully registered and provides a button to navigate to the member top page.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the immediate reassurance of seeing the registration success message and the choice of whether to explore your new account dashboard.

dating.task: set up and use a dating app or site (Tinder, Bumble, Hinge, Match, OkCupid): create or edit the profile with photos and prompts, set preferences and filters, browse candidates and act on them, and reach a match or send a first message where the flow allows; complete when the match screen or the sent first message is shown. Surface pinned: the dating product itself — not dating-advice talking-head content, not story-time videos about dates.

tree.label: Meet someone through an app
tree.note: do 1, then 2 and 3 - the signup wizards run them interleaved as one screen sequence (3ltT, 17j1, MpoY), and five keepers arrive with all of it already done (Nmjb, 2Xie, FWwo, AOCl, Jzez). then 4. 2 is re-entered from 4 whenever the app nags for photos, gates content on completeness, or the profile is itself the thing being tested (Nmjb, FWwo, 3yWz). 5 is entered from 4.6, 6.2 and 7.1, never on its own. 6 after time passes with the app closed - 8 hours in Nmjb, 24 in 1D06, 48 twice in MpoY. then 7, then back to 4 or 6 for another round. 8 when a conversation moves to a phone number, or when the app comes off the phone.

questions.question: Should you check the suggested profile, or go to your own profile first?

questions.question: What password do you want to set for your new account?

questions.question: Is this the correct dating app to open?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to personally verify the authenticity and safety of the app being installed and opened.

questions.question: Do you want to allow the app to send you notifications?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means the agent decides whether this app is allowed to interrupt your daily life with alerts and badges.

questions.question: Should you link an external account for easier login?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means the agent decides whether to link your external accounts, which impacts your privacy and account recovery options.

questions.question: Do you want to sign in to an existing account or create a new one?

questions.question: Is the default country code correct for your phone number?
questions.why: Selecting the correct country code ensures you can successfully receive the SMS verification codes and account alerts mentioned on the screen.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to ensure the correct international dialing code is selected for your specific mobile device.

questions.question: Which phone number should I enter?
questions.why: The screen explicitly states that entering your number means you agree to receive text messages about your account, including verification codes and match updates.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to decide which phone number is linked to your dating profile and exposed to potentially frequent SMS notifications.

questions.question: What is the 6-digit verification code sent to your phone?
questions.why: The screen requires the six-digit code sent via text message to verify the phone number and continue the login process.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step requires granting the agent access to your personal text messages to retrieve the security code.

questions.question: Do you agree to Tinder's House Rules?
questions.why: The app requires you to accept its community guidelines regarding authenticity, safety, and respect before allowing you to proceed with account creation.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally review and commit to the platform's behavioral expectations and safety guidelines.

questions.question: Do you agree to the terms and data usage policies to finalize your profile?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the chance to read the specific privacy terms and make an informed choice about how their dating data is shared.

questions.question: What first name do you want to display on your profile, knowing it cannot be changed later?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to choose how they are permanently identified to potential matches on the platform.

questions.question: Should I keep your pre-filled Facebook name and gender identity, or edit them for your dating profile?

devicesetup.task: set up a new device through its companion app or on-device flow: a new phone (setup, account sign-in, data transfer), a router or mesh Wi-Fi via its app, a smartwatch pairing, or a smart-home device (camera, plug, speaker, doorbell): the unbox-to-working arc — pair or connect, sign in, configure the essentials; complete when the device shows working/connected in the app or the phone reaches its fully set-up home screen. Surface pinned: the setup flow itself — not unboxing-only or review videos.

tree.note: do 1, then 2. phone routes then do 3 and 4, where 4.3 is the whole of 4. accessory routes do 4 first, then 2.5 to 2.8, then 3 - the app will not look for a device until it knows the account. then 5 where anything is carried over; uSN0 and DT4C's first pass skip it outright. then 6. 7 always, and 7.9 when 7 comes back wrong. 8 on the transfer routes, reaching into 1.10 where the erase is actually run (aawv). 9 where the device has services to configure - fok5 and NZzD do parts of it inside 6, u--l does all of it after 7.

dmv.task: renew a driver's license or vehicle registration on a state DMV portal: verify identity and eligibility, work through the renewal form, pay the fee; complete when the renewal-submitted confirmation — receipt or temporary document — is on screen. Surface pinned: a state DMV web portal, not an in-office visit vlog. Variants: address change (seeded variant), first-time license applications, REAL ID upgrades, and driving-test booking do not belong.

ebay.task: bid on an eBay auction as a buyer: find an auction listing, review item condition, seller rating, and shipping, place a bid by setting a maximum bid, confirm the bid, and see the resulting bid status; complete when the bid-confirmed state ("You're the highest bidder" or "You've been outbid") is on screen. Surface pinned: the eBay website or app. Variants: selling or listing items, dropshipping/reselling content, "Buy It Now" only purchases (that is ordinary shopping), and sniping-tool promotions do not belong.

questions.question: Are the bid amounts and total number of bids consistent throughout the process?
questions.why: The screen shows the current bid logically increasing from $42.00 with 11 bids to a final winning bid of $46.00 with 16 bids.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to monitor the live competitiveness and logical progression of the auction.

questions.question: Did the auction end with no bid recorded from this account?
questions.why: The screen showed the auction countdown reaching zero and ending before any bid amount was entered or the Place bid button was clicked.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to win the item because the agent failed to submit the bid before the auction ended.

children.label: Recover from an outbid
children.note: entered from the red notice, at any distance from the close - seconds after 6.6 (s_CE, 08WT) or inside a live hold (B7Zu, T5mb). 7.1 then 7.2, looping until the lead holds or the clock kills it - 08WT cycles three times, T5mb runs it inside the final 25 seconds and still loses. 7.3 closes each cycle.

questions.question: Is the bid amount you entered valid and ready to submit?
questions.why: A red exclamation mark in the input field indicates that the entered value of '208.1' has an invalid format or increment.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to correct a formatting error before submission, which could cause your bid to be rejected by the system.

questions.question: Does the page say another bidder's maximum is above yours?
questions.why: The screen shows a warning that another bidder's maximum bid exceeded yours, requiring a decision on whether to submit a higher amount.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally evaluate your budget limit in real-time when deciding if the item is still worth the higher price.

questions.question: Did your bid put you in the lead, and what's the current price?
questions.why: Verifying the confirmation message and current bid amount ensures your maximum bid was accepted and you are currently winning the auction.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the immediate reassurance of seeing your winning status and knowing exactly how much of your maximum bid is currently being used.

children.label: Verify the outcome
children.note: 8.1 while seconds remain, 8.2 at zero - the won state often needs a reload to appear. 8.3 whenever the auction resolves; 8.4 is one keeper's full audit. a loss ends the task here (T5mb, dh72, GYkw).

questions.question: Did you actually confirm the bid, or is the item already sold?
questions.why: The screen shows a 'SOLD' badge and a final price, contradicting the narrator's claim that a bid was confirmed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user would falsely believe they have an active bid on the item when it has actually already been sold to someone else.

questions.question: Do you see the exact phrase 'You won this auction' on the screen?
questions.why: Assuming the auction is won when the screen only confirms you are the highest bidder misrepresents the actual outcome shown.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses accurate tracking of their auction if the agent falsely reports a final win instead of a pending highest-bidder status.

questions.question: Does the page say you won, and what is the final price?
questions.why: The screen displays a 'Congratulations! You won this item' banner along with the final price of US $0.31.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses confirmation of their auction victory and the knowledge of the final purchase price.

questions.question: Does the final bid price logically follow from your maximum bid and the previous current bid?
questions.why: The final price of $0.31 is consistent with a maximum bid of $0.66 and a previous high bid of $0.30, confirming the automatic bidding system worked correctly.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to verify that the platform's automatic bidding system executed their bid correctly without overcharging.

questions.question: How close to the end of the auction did you place your winning bid?
questions.why: Comparing the recorded bid time of 10:12:17 to the auction end time of 10:12:20 confirms exactly how narrow your margin of victory was.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the strategic insight and personal satisfaction of knowing exactly how close to the final deadline their successful bid was recorded.

children.label: Close out the win
children.note: 9.1 on every win. 9.2 and 9.3 where the buyer bothers; 9.4 loops back to 2 when the session hunts more - Zkom six times, fx1m until a three-win quota releases the fourth. no keeper in the corpus completes a payment.

questions.question: Is the checkout total shown, with shipping, the amount you want to pay?
questions.why: The checkout screen displays a total of $347.64 for the three items, which represents your final financial commitment.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to personally verify that the final combined cost aligns with their budget before the order is confirmed.

questions.question: Do you actually see a checkout page displaying the total order amount, or just multiple item pages?
questions.why: This matters because the screen at 1:39 only shows four panes of eBay item pages, contradicting the claim that a checkout page with a $347.64 total is visible.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses accurate verification of their final costs if the agent hallucinates a checkout page and order total that do not actually exist on the screen.

questions.question: Should you confirm this bid for a fourth item, or cancel it since you have already won three?
questions.why: The confirmation popup shows your $120.55 max bid, providing a final opportunity to click the 'X' and cancel if you have already acquired enough of these items.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might automatically confirm the bid without realizing you already won enough of this item, resulting in unnecessary spending.

questions.question: Are the current search results showing the most up-to-date auctions ending soonest?
questions.why: Refreshing the search results for 'pcs' ensures you are looking at the most current listings and accurate time remaining, as auction statuses change rapidly.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to guarantee the agent is acting on real-time auction data rather than stale search results.

email.task: compose and send an email in a mail client (Gmail, Outlook, Yahoo Mail, Apple Mail): open compose, address the recipient, write the subject and body, optionally attach a file, send it, and verify it in Sent; complete when the message shows as sent. Surface pinned: the mail client's compose-and-send flow — not inbox-organizing tours, not newsletter/marketing tools, not email-etiquette advice videos.

tree.label: Send an email
tree.note: 1 when the client is not already open and signed in - most keepers start authenticated and skip most of it. then 2: a new message, or a reply or forward entered from 8.1 (DFXu, ycKB, 6rzA, 0D7H, zCsj), which decides how much of 3 is left to do. 3 and 4 in either order - HnFK writes the subject and body before the recipient. 5 where the message carries a file; 5.4 only when the client refuses the file, and it returns into 5.2 or 5.5 once the file is ready (UehN never gets back). then 6, one of 6.2 to 6.5; 6.6 and 6.7 where the client interrupts. then 7 - in this corpus that's where the task actually completes, and 7 is skipped by seven keepers. 8 at any point.

children.label: Get into the mailbox
children.note: 1.1 then 1.2. 1.3 only from a logged-out start - two keepers. 1.4 where more than one account is signed in. 1.5 and 1.6 as orientation before any composing, and only on the videos that tour the client.

questions.question: Which app do you open to access your email?
questions.why: The home screen displays multiple applications, so you must select the specific mail client you want to use to send the message.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to choose which specific email client or account is used to send the message.

questions.question: The page is asking you to sign in — do you want to enter your password yourself?
questions.why: The sign-in screen requires an email and password, which can be typed manually or autofilled using a password manager.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide whether to securely autofill your credentials using a specific password manager or type them manually.

questions.question: Which email account are you currently sending from?
questions.why: Opening the profile pop-up reveals the active email address, '[email]', ensuring the message is sent from the correct account.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to verify or switch their sender identity before composing the message.

children.label: Open a compose surface
children.note: 2.1 for a new message. 2.2 and 2.3 instead when the message answers one that arrived, entered from 8.1 - and that choice sets what 3 has left to do: reply-all arrives with To and Cc filled, forward arrives with To empty and quoted history attached. 2.4 after the draft exists. 2.5 where the compose surface is a panel that can be resized. 2.6 before typing, on the two keepers that tour the surface first.

questions.question: Did the forward open with the original message included?
questions.why: Clicking the 'Forward' link below the thread automatically populates a new compose window with the original message and a 'Fwd:' subject line.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide whether to forward the existing thread or summarize the information in a brand new email.

questions.question: Should you change the response type to Reply, Reply All, or Forward?
questions.why: The screen shows a dropdown menu that lets you switch the current draft between a direct reply, a reply to all, or a forward.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to manually control exactly which participants from the original email thread will receive your message.

children.label: Set the recipients
children.note: 3.1 in nearly every keeper - typing resolved by a suggestion is close to universal here. 3.2 where the address is not in the list. 3.3 to reach the copy fields, then 3.4 and 3.5 where the message needs them. 3.6 replaces all of it on a bulk send, and rules 3.3 to 3.5 out. 3.7 whenever a chip is wrong. 3.8 before trusting a group. reply-all routes arrive with this goal already done (DFXu).

questions.question: This draft goes to several people as one message — one email to all, or a separate copy to each?
questions.why: The screen shows a single draft addressed to multiple recipients with a generic 'Hey' greeting, which prevents addressing each person by their actual name.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the personal touch of addressing each recipient by name, which makes the mass invitation feel less genuine.

questions.question: Which email address should you select as the recipient?
questions.why: The screen displays a list of multiple available email accounts, so you must select the correct one to ensure the message reaches the intended person.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means the agent might select the wrong recipient from the list, potentially sending your message to an unintended contact.

questions.question: What exact email address are you entering in the 'To' field?
questions.why: Entering the precise email address in the 'To' field ensures the message reaches the correct person instead of bouncing or going to a stranger.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the chance to personally verify that the recipient's address is typed perfectly to avoid sending the message to the wrong person.

questions.question: Who should you add as a Cc recipient?
questions.why: The dropdown suggests contacts like 'Woggle Spy Lucinda' based on your typing, requiring you to select the correct person to keep in the loop.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose the ability to decide exactly who needs visibility into the conversation without being the primary recipient.

questions.question: When replying to a thread, does the recipient list still include everyone from the original?
questions.why: Confirming that the visible names and the '+1' indicator match the three original Cc recipients ensures no one is accidentally dropped from the thread.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the assurance that all necessary stakeholders are kept in the loop on the communication.

questions.question: Who should you blind carbon copy on this email?
questions.why: The screen shows an autocomplete dropdown with multiple contacts like Woggle Spy Cynthia and Woggle Spy Cuthbert for the Bcc field, requiring a choice of who should secretly receive the message.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means the agent might blind copy the wrong contact, potentially failing to keep the right person confidentially informed.

children.label: Build a bulk recipient list
children.note: 3.6.2 first - the feature has to be switched on before anything else changes. then 3.6.1, and one of 3.6.3 or the pair 3.6.4 and 3.6.5. 3.6.6 is read after the fact in this keeper, not before.

questions.question: Should you use the mail merge option to add recipients from a spreadsheet?
questions.why: Clicking the mail merge icon revealed a dropdown to add recipients from a spreadsheet, which fundamentally changes how the email is addressed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to decide whether to automate addressing a mass email using a spreadsheet or to enter recipients manually.

questions.question: Which contacts do you want to include in this mail merge?
questions.why: The 'Select contacts' modal offers individual selection or a 'Select All' option for the three available contacts.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to hand-pick exactly which of your contacts should receive the message.

questions.question: Which spreadsheet contains the recipient data?
questions.why: The screen showed a 'Link a spreadsheet for recipient info' dialog displaying recent files like 'School Fees', requiring a choice of data source.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses control over which contact list is used, risking sending the email to the wrong group of people.

questions.question: Which columns from the spreadsheet will you use to personalize the email?
questions.why: Reviewing the 'School Fees' sheet ensures you know exactly which fields, like 'Amount Due' and 'Account Number', are available to insert into the message.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose the opportunity to manually verify that the data source contains all the necessary and correct fields before generating the emails.

questions.question: Did the client block or warn about the send because of an account sending limit?
questions.why: Gmail restricts standard accounts to 500 outgoing messages and mail merge to 1,500 recipients per day, meaning exceeding these limits will block your emails from sending.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the awareness of your account's specific sending thresholds, which could result in a blocked campaign if the agent blindly exceeds the limit.

questions.question: Does the page say mail merge disables a feature this message needs, like Cc or scheduling?
questions.why: The help page explicitly states that using a spreadsheet for mail merge prevents you from adding Cc or Bcc recipients and disables features like schedule send and confidential mode.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to weigh whether the convenience of a spreadsheet outweighs the need to copy other recipients or schedule the email.

questions.question: Is the intended contact group available to select in the dropdown?
questions.why: Seeing the 'Test Group' entry with its member count in the autocomplete dropdown confirms the mail client recognizes your pre-made distribution list.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you cannot visually verify the group's member count to ensure the exact right list of people will receive your message.

questions.question: Who does the contact group actually expand to?
questions.why: Checking the details pane for 'Test Group' ensures you know exactly which email addresses, like Christian and Dad, will receive the message.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the peace of mind of manually reviewing and confirming the exact individuals included in a group alias before the email goes out.

children.label: Write the message
children.note: 4.1 then 4.2 - HnFK does both before the recipient. 4.3 where the client suggests text mid-typing. 4.4 only where the content comes from another application. 4.5 on a forward, before the quoted history travels with it. 4.6 once per field the spreadsheet supplies. 4.7 is opened in three keepers and applied in one.

questions.question: What date, time, and duration should you set for the scheduled meeting?
questions.why: The 'Schedule Meeting' window requires you to configure the 'Topic', 'Start' date and time, and 'Duration' to generate the correct invitation details.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the control to pick a specific date and time that perfectly aligns with your unwritten scheduling preferences.

questions.question: Should I use your Personal Meeting ID or generate one automatically, and do you want to require a password?
questions.why: The screen shows options to either generate a meeting ID automatically or use a Personal Meeting ID, along with a checkbox to require a meeting password.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to balance convenience and security for their specific meeting participants.

questions.question: What should you enter as the subject of the email?
questions.why: The screen shows an empty 'Subject:' field that requires a concise summary of the email's purpose.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to craft a specific subject line that sets the right tone and context for your recipient.

questions.question: What do you want to write in the message body?
questions.why: The 'Compose email' field is where the actual content and details of your message must be entered.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose control over the exact wording, tone, and specific details communicated to the recipient.

questions.question: Should you interact with the Smart Compose tooltip or ignore it and type your message manually?
questions.why: The screen displays a Smart Compose tooltip offering writing suggestions that can be acknowledged, disabled, or simply ignored while drafting.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose the choice of whether to utilize, dismiss, or permanently disable the AI writing suggestions for your account.

questions.question: Do the generated meeting invitation details read back correctly before they are copied into the email?
questions.why: The 'Zoom - Schedule Meeting' dialog offers options to open with a default calendar or copy to the clipboard.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to review the meeting details before they are copied and sent.

questions.question: Should you keep or delete the forwarded email history below your new message?
questions.why: The screen shows the previous email thread appended below the new message, which might clutter the email or include unnecessary context.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to curate the email's context and ensure the recipient only sees the relevant information you intended to share.

questions.question: Which merge tag do you want to use for the greeting?
questions.why: The screen shows a menu of mail merge tags like '@ firstname' and '@ lastname', which determines how the recipient's name will be formatted in the automated greeting.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The delegator loses control over the tone of the email by not being able to choose between a casual first name or a more formal full name greeting.

questions.question: Are all the purple placeholder tags correctly positioned in your draft?
questions.why: Verifying the purple highlight tags like '@firstname' and '@amountdue' ensures the mail merge will populate the correct data for each recipient before you click Continue.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally verify that sensitive merge fields like account numbers and amounts due are placed in the correct context within the message.

children.label: Attach a file
children.note: 5.1 opens the source list, and which sources exist is the client's decision, not the user's. then 5.2, or 5.3 where the file is dragged in instead, or 5.5 where it lives in cloud storage. 5.4 fires when the client refuses what was picked, and returns into 5.2 or 5.5 once the file is ready. 5.6 where the upload has to finish before anything else. three keepers open 5.1 and attach nothing at all.

questions.question: Do you need to attach any files or Drive links to this email?
questions.why: The compose toolbar displays icons for attaching local files or inserting from Google Drive, prompting a choice about including supplementary documents.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the ability to judge whether additional context or specific documents should accompany your message.

questions.question: Which source should you select from the Attach File dropdown?
questions.why: The dropdown offers recent items, web locations, and the local PC, so you must specify where the intended file is currently stored.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide exactly which storage location to pull the attachment from, risking the selection of an incorrect or outdated version of the file.

questions.question: Which file do you select to attach to the email?
questions.why: Choosing the correct file from the Downloads folder ensures the intended image, such as 'Cool Guy.jpg', is attached to the email.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to manually browse your folders and visually verify you are attaching the exact file you intended.

questions.question: Can the file you asked for be found where you said it was?
questions.why: The file manager displays multiple image directories like Camera, Downloads, and Canva, so you must know exactly where the intended attachment is saved.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means losing the ability to visually browse your personal folders to find the exact image you intended to share.

questions.question: Do you want to resize the inline image?
questions.why: The screen shows options like 'Small' and 'Best fit' to control how the inline image appears within the email body.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to visually verify the image's layout and choose the best fit for the recipient's reading experience.

children.label: Prepare the file elsewhere
children.note: 5.4.1 names what stopped it. then whichever of 5.4.2 to 5.4.5 the block calls for: a folder gets compressed, an oversized file gets uploaded, a cloud file gets its sharing set, a cloud file that has to travel as bytes gets downloaded first. 5.4.6 where the client is not connected to the storage service at all. 5.4.3 after any compression. then back into 5.2 or 5.5 - UehN is the one keeper that never gets back.

questions.question: Do you want to use Mail Drop to send this oversized attachment?
questions.why: The attachment is 56.3 MB, which exceeds the 52.4 MB limit, prompting Apple Mail to offer iCloud delivery.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to choose whether your file is temporarily hosted on iCloud or sent directly through your email provider.

questions.question: Can you attach an entire folder directly to the email?
questions.why: Selecting a folder and clicking 'Open' in the file browser merely opens it to reveal contents like 'road-259815_1280.jpg' rather than attaching the folder itself.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the awareness that folders cannot be attached directly and must either be zipped or have their individual files selected.

questions.question: Which folder needs to be compressed?
questions.why: The screen shows a File Explorer window with 'Folder To Be Emailed', which must be selected and compressed before it can be attached.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to specify exactly which folder should be prepared and attached to the email.

questions.question: Is the option to compress the folder available in this context menu?
questions.why: The context menu for the Zoom folder lacks a compress or zip option, which is necessary because most email clients require folders to be zipped before attaching.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to decide whether to troubleshoot the missing compression tool or simply abandon this folder and attach a different one.

questions.question: Are these the correct files to compress and attach?
questions.why: The screen showed the contents of 'Folder To Be Emailed', allowing verification of the files before zipping them for the email.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the visual confirmation that all intended files are present in the folder before it gets compressed and sent.

questions.question: Is there a new .zip file where the folder was?
questions.why: Confirming the completion notification and locating the new .zip file in the directory ensures the folder is actually ready to be attached.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the visual reassurance of seeing the newly created .zip file appear in your directory before it gets attached.

questions.question: Should you allow the browser to upload the entire folder?
questions.why: The browser explicitly asks if you trust the site before allowing the upload of all 10 files from the selected folder.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally assess the security warning and explicitly grant the site access to your local files.

questions.question: Is the file you want to attach already uploaded to your Google Drive?
questions.why: The Google Drive file picker displayed 'No files found,' indicating that the file must be uploaded to Drive first before it can be attached.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to manually locate their local file and upload it to Drive when the agent gets stuck on an empty file picker.

questions.question: Do you want the recipient to be able to download the attached file?
questions.why: The Google Drive preview window shows a 'Download' button, indicating the current permissions allow the recipient to save the file locally.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to control the specific access and download permissions for the file they are sharing.

questions.question: Which Google account do you want to use to sign in to Yahoo Mail?
questions.why: The screen prompts you to "Choose an account" to "continue to Yahoo!", which determines the sender identity for your email.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to ensure the email is sent from your preferred primary account rather than an alternate or work account.

questions.question: Should I grant Yahoo permission to access and modify my Google Drive files?
questions.why: The authorization screen warns that Yahoo will be able to see, edit, create, and delete all of your Google Drive files.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the chance to evaluate whether they trust the email client with extensive access to their personal cloud storage.

questions.question: Should I insert the file as a Drive link or as a direct attachment?
questions.why: The file selection modal provides 'Insert as' options at the bottom right to send either a Drive link or an actual Attachment.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to choose the most accessible file delivery method for your specific recipient.

questions.question: Has the file finished uploading to the email draft?
questions.why: Sending the email before the progress bar for the zip file disappears could result in the message going out without the attachment.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the visual confirmation that your specific file successfully uploaded without errors before the message was sent.

children.label: Send or save the message
children.note: 6.1 first in the keepers that check anything. then exactly one of 6.2 to 6.5 - the four ways a draft ends here. 6.6 where the client refuses to proceed as-is. 6.7 when a cloud attachment forces a second commit before delivery. 6.8 to read whatever comes back. eight keepers produce no evidenced commit at all.

questions.question: Does the greeting in the email body match the recipient's email address?
questions.why: The recipient field shows [email], but the message body addresses 'James', indicating a mismatch before sending.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user risks sending an email to the wrong person or confusing the recipient with an incorrect greeting.

questions.question: Do the links in the draft exactly match the ones in the source document?
questions.why: The screen showed different video IDs in the final Gmail draft compared to the original Google Doc.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the assurance that the correct information is being sent to the recipient when the agent alters or miscopies the provided links.

questions.question: Ready to send — recipient, subject, message, and attachment all as you want them?
questions.why: The compose window shows 'Cool Guy.jpg' successfully attached at the bottom, indicating the message is complete and ready for dispatch.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the final opportunity to verify that the correct file was attached before the email is irreversibly sent.

questions.question: What date and time should I schedule this email to send?
questions.why: The 'Pick date & time' dialog requires a specific calendar day and time to ensure the message arrives exactly when intended.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose the ability to strategically time the email's arrival, such as right before a scheduled meeting.

questions.question: Should you check 'Don't show again' before clicking 'Got it' on the junk mail warning?
questions.why: The dialog box offers a choice to permanently dismiss future warnings about email best practices by checking a box before proceeding.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to decide whether they want to be reminded of email best practices in the future.

questions.question: Should you send a preview email to yourself before sending it to the whole list?
questions.why: The 'Ready to send' dialog offers a 'Send preview' option to verify the formatting before dispatching the separate emails to your recipients.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Letting an agent automatically skip the preview removes your final chance to catch formatting errors or mistakes before the emails reach your recipients.

questions.question: Do you want to send this email without a subject?
questions.why: The mail client displayed a 'Missing subject' warning, requiring a choice between sending the email as-is or returning to the draft to add one.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means losing the opportunity to decide whether a blank subject line is acceptable for this specific recipient or if it looks too unprofessional.

questions.question: How should you set the access permissions for the linked Google Drive file?
questions.why: The dialog requires choosing between restricting access to specific people or allowing anyone with the link to view the file.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose control over balancing file security against the recipient's convenience when accessing the attachment.

questions.question: Do you see a 'Sending...' notification confirming the action is in progress?
questions.why: The black 'Sending...' toast at the bottom of the inbox screen confirms the app registered the send command and is actively processing the email.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might close the app immediately after clicking send rather than waiting for completion, which could interrupt the process and leave the email stuck in the outbox.

questions.question: Did you see the 'Message sent' confirmation banner?
questions.why: The bottom-left banner changing from 'Sending...' to 'Message sent' confirms the email was successfully dispatched.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you miss the brief window to click 'Undo' if you suddenly realize you made a mistake in the email.

children.label: Confirm the message went
children.note: 7.1 first - the toast is not treated as sufficient, and three keepers open the folder straight after seeing one. 7.2 when the message is not where it should be. 7.3 where the client filed it somewhere else. 7.4 in the six keepers that go and look at the receiving end. seven keepers stop at the toast or before it.

questions.question: Is this message in the Sent folder?
questions.why: Checking the Sent folder after seeing the 'Message sent' notification confirms that the message and its attachments were actually dispatched.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the peace of mind of visually confirming that the exact message and its attachments are safely logged in your sent history.

questions.question: Are the recipient, subject, body, and attachment correct in the sent message?
questions.why: Reviewing the sent message details, including the recipient, text, and image thumbnail, confirms the email was transmitted exactly as intended.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the peace of mind of personally confirming that the correct message and file actually went to the right person.

questions.question: Did your email send, or is it stuck in the outbox?
questions.why: The Sent folder did not show the recent email and instead displayed a banner for unsent messages in the Outbox, indicating a delivery issue that needs to be investigated.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the certainty of knowing whether your message actually reached the recipient or if it silently failed to send.

questions.question: Is your email correctly queued in the Scheduled folder with the right contents?
questions.why: Checking the Scheduled folder and the banner inside the email confirms your message is queued to go out at the exact time you intended.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the peace of mind of personally verifying the scheduled time and contents before the delayed send occurs.

children.label: Check the receiving end
children.note: 7.4.1, then 7.4.2 where it has not landed yet, then 7.4.3. 7.4.4 where the point of the message was the file.

questions.question: Do you see the new email in the inbox?
questions.why: The screen shows a new email from 'me' with the subject 'Leave letter', confirming the message was delivered.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the immediate reassurance of personally verifying that the email successfully reached its destination.

questions.question: Does the shared link open without requiring sign-in?
questions.why: The screen shows the recipient clicking the Google Drive link in the email to confirm the file opens successfully without requiring a login.
