questions.question: Should you include nearby airports in your search?
questions.why: The departure field includes a checkbox to add nearby airports, which expands flight options but might require additional ground travel.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to decide if the inconvenience of traveling to an alternative nearby airport is worth the potential savings or better flight times.

questions.question: Do you want to search for fares using cash or miles?
questions.why: The search form includes a 'Shop with Miles' checkbox that must be selected before hitting search to see reward redemptions instead of cash prices.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to decide whether to spend their accumulated frequent flyer miles or pay cash for this specific itinerary.

questions.question: What route, dates, and passengers is the search about to run with?
questions.why: Verifying the one-way route from Manila to Boracay on October 11 for one adult ensures the search returns the right flight options.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the chance to double-check their specific travel dates and destination before the search is executed.

children.label: Pick the flights
children.note: 3.1 or 3.2 when the search comes back dead - 3.1 goes back to 2, 3.2 stays on the results. 3.3 wherever a grid or ribbon prices the neighboring days. 3.4 and 3.5 where used at all - most keepers skip both. 3.6 rides on the results list; 3.7 vets a candidate. 3.8, then 3.9 on round trips - except where one card carries both legs and 3.9 never fires (Q4Km, DTJW, xE7S).

questions.question: Should you book this flight now or wait, based on the price prediction?
questions.why: The screen displays a price prediction stating 'Prices are unlikely to drop', advising you on whether it is safe to book now or better to wait.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the benefit of the platform's historical data analysis, potentially waiting for a price drop that won't happen and risking a price increase instead.

questions.question: Do you want to toggle on price tracking for this route instead of buying today?
questions.why: The interface displays a 'Tracked prices' option that allows you to receive notifications if the fare drops for your searched dates.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to passively monitor the route for a better deal if you aren't ready to commit to purchasing the flight right now.

questions.question: Do you want to abandon the current search and start over?
questions.why: The screen shows a confirmation dialog asking if you want to end your transaction and return to the homepage, which will erase your current progress.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide whether to preserve your current flight selections or discard them to begin a completely new search.

questions.question: Has the session expired and released the held fare?
questions.why: Flight booking systems only hold inventory and pricing for a strict time limit (often 10-15 minutes) before expiring the session and releasing the fare back to the public.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to decide whether to restart the search from scratch or abandon the booking if the original fare is no longer available after a timeout.

questions.question: Which alternative return date should you pick if your preferred date has no flights?
questions.why: The screen displayed a yellow warning banner indicating no flights were found for the initially selected date, requiring a choice among the remaining available dates and their respective fares.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means losing the personal ability to weigh the schedule and price trade-offs of alternative travel dates when the ideal itinerary is unavailable.

questions.question: Do you want to adjust your departure date to get a cheaper fare?
questions.why: The date carousel shows that departing on Sunday, 12 May is significantly cheaper than Friday or Saturday.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to weigh the cost savings against your personal schedule flexibility.

questions.question: Which filters, if any, should you apply to narrow down the search results?
questions.why: The screen shows 716 total results alongside summary cards and sidebar filters, making this the moment to decide how to narrow down the options.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally weigh trade-offs between price, duration, and convenience when filtering a large list of flights.

questions.question: Which airlines do you want to include in the search results?
questions.why: The sidebar allows you to filter the flight options by specific carriers like WestJet or Flair Airlines to suit your preferences.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to manually include or exclude specific airlines based on your personal past experiences or loyalty memberships.

questions.question: Should you rely on the default ranking for price and convenience, or adjust the sorting options to find the best flight?
questions.why: The screen defaults to ranking flights by a mix of price and convenience, requiring a choice on whether to trust this order or explore other sorting methods.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might just select the top recommended flight, missing your personal preferences for balancing cost, layovers, and specific airlines.

questions.question: Do you want to sort the flight results by carbon emissions?
questions.why: The 'Sort by' dropdown includes an 'Emissions' option, allowing you to prioritize greener flights over the cheapest or fastest routes.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to align your travel choices with your environmental values if the agent only optimizes for price or duration.

questions.question: Do the outbound and return legs use different airports in the same city?
questions.why: The screen displays a direct round trip for C$ 340 involving different Toronto-area airports, requiring you to confirm if these specific logistics fit your travel plans.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally weigh the convenience of the specific flight times and airport locations against the ticket price.

questions.question: Does this itinerary require a self-transfer or separate tickets that leave you unprotected if a flight is delayed?
questions.why: Aggregators often bundle separate one-way tickets on different airlines to save money, meaning you must collect and re-check baggage yourself and are not protected if the first leg is delayed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The agent might book a risky 'hacker fare' to save a few dollars, leaving you stranded and forced to buy a new same-day ticket out of pocket if you miss the connection.

questions.question: Which flight should you select from the search results?
questions.why: You need to evaluate the different departure times and prices, such as the ₹4,049 morning flight versus the ₹4,200 evening flight, to find the best option.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally balance your schedule preferences against the specific price differences shown.

questions.question: Which returning flight should you select?
questions.why: The screen showed multiple return options from Boracay to Manila, such as an earlier flight for PHP 3,954.68 and a later, cheaper one for PHP 2,900.76.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means losing the ability to balance your preferred departure time against the cost savings of a cheaper ticket.

children.label: Choose where to book
children.note: 4.1 with 4.2 against it, then 4.3. 4.4 when the first provider disappoints, looping back through 4.1 (DTJW). 4.5 right after landing - the two keepers who run it are the two that catch the handoff changing the numbers. only the metasearch keepers run this goal at all; airline-direct and single-OTA paths never see it.

questions.question: Which booking provider should you select to purchase this ticket?
questions.why: The screen lists multiple booking agencies with varying prices alongside a warning to check for extra fees and terms.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to balance the lowest fare against the reliability and specific terms of the third-party booking agency.

questions.question: Did the handoff land on the seller that was chosen?
questions.why: The interstitial screen requires clicking 'Continue to booking' to successfully redirect from the search aggregator to the final booking site.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the awareness of being handed off to a third-party booking site to complete your reservation.

questions.question: Does the price on the booking site match the aggregator's quote?
questions.why: This matters because the initial Skyscanner screen listed the total as 126 €, but the subsequent Mytrip redirect screen displayed €125.99.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might ignore price discrepancies during redirects, preventing you from catching potential bait-and-switch pricing tactics from third-party sites.

questions.question: Does the itinerary on the booking site match the flight picked on the aggregator?
questions.why: Verifying the Mumbai to New Delhi flight times and the 15 kg baggage allowance ensures you selected the right itinerary before providing personal information.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the chance to catch a mistake in the departure time or baggage limit before committing your personal details to the reservation.

children.label: Choose the fare tier
children.note: 5.1 then 5.2 - per leg where the site asks per leg (MasT, lc1q, Q4Km, 15Vk), once for the whole trip where it does not (d2oz, WZ5A, CtaK). 5.3 when a cheap pick triggers a defense modal (DTJW). WZ5A re-enters here from the bags step through the stepper's Change fare, and never comes back.

questions.question: Do the benefits promised on the initial fare card match what is shown in the fare comparison table?
questions.why: The SpiceFlex fare card at 1:14 promises unlimited date changes and a preferred seat, but the comparison table at 1:52 shows these features are not actually included.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to catch conflicting fare terms and avoid paying extra for a premium tier that fails to deliver the promised benefits.

questions.question: Is the fare bundle a better deal than buying a checked bag separately?
questions.why: The bundle costs $81.16 more than the base fare, but since a 20kg bag alone is $57.32, you must decide if the included seat and meal are worth the extra $23.84.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to calculate the true cost of individual perks and decide if the bundled extras are worth the premium over a la carte pricing.

questions.question: Which fare tier offers the right balance of price and flexibility for your trip?
questions.why: The screen displays multiple fare options like Economy Semi Flex for 687 USD with change fees versus Eco Flex with free changes, requiring a choice based on your need for flexibility.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide whether saving money upfront is worth the risk of paying higher change or cancellation fees later.

questions.question: Do you want to pay to upgrade the fare you already chose, or keep it?
questions.why: The screen explicitly warns that the Saver ticket has no flexibility and charges a 30 € fee for later changes, offering a Standard upgrade for 49.17 €.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might automatically buy the upgrade to avoid penalty risks, spending extra money you would have preferred to save.

children.label: Enter the passenger details
children.note: 6.1 or 6.2 per passenger; 6.3 and 6.4 as the form asks. then 6.5. 6.6 when the submit fails - twice triggered on purpose, once by silent state loss.

questions.question: Does the selected saved profile match the traveler being booked?
questions.why: Choosing the correct pre-existing profile ensures the booking details match the traveler's ID exactly without manual entry.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to specify exactly which of their saved contacts is traveling on this ticket.

questions.question: Do the name, date of birth, and gender entered match the passenger's passport exactly?
questions.why: The screen requires your exact name, date of birth, and gender to issue a valid ticket, while offering optional fields for frequent flyer numbers and special requests.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to ensure their name matches their passport exactly and the opportunity to attach their frequent flyer account to the booking.

questions.question: Does your passport have as long left on it as the page requires?
questions.why: The screen displays a warning to ensure the passenger's travel document has at least a 4-month validity, which is a strict requirement for this specific trip.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to realize their passport might expire too soon, which would result in being denied boarding despite having a valid ticket.

questions.question: Do you want to add a frequent flyer number?
questions.why: The form includes optional fields for a frequent flyer program and number, which allows you to earn miles for the trip.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: If the agent skips this step without asking, you miss out on earning miles or loyalty points for your flight.

questions.question: Do you need to add your GST details for this booking?
questions.why: The passenger information form includes an optional section to enter GST details, which is necessary if you intend to claim a tax credit for a business trip.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might skip this optional field, causing you to lose the ability to claim the flight as a tax-deductible business expense.

questions.question: Who do you want to set as the main contact for booking confirmations and updates?
questions.why: The screen requires selecting a main contact from a dropdown to auto-fill the email and phone number for trip notifications.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to choose which specific traveler receives the booking confirmation and critical flight updates.

questions.question: Do you want to opt into SMS and email notifications before continuing?
questions.why: The screen presents checkboxes to allow notifications via SMS and email before you click Continue to proceed with the USD 2,971.60 booking.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to protect your privacy and decline optional marketing messages by leaving the boxes unchecked.

questions.question: Does every filled field match the traveler's actual details?
questions.why: Verifying your contact information before clicking 'Continue' ensures the 3,025,311 NGN trip is booked under the correct passenger details.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to double-check your personal information for typos before the agent advances to the seat selection step.

questions.question: Why did your form submission fail, and which passenger profile must you select to proceed?
questions.why: The form will not advance to the next step until you scroll up and select a required passenger profile like 'deborah abioye'.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to ensure the correct saved passenger profile is chosen when resolving the form submission error.

children.label: Add or decline the extras
children.note: 7.1 to 7.5 in whatever order the site's stepper runs them; every child is a priced offer and most keepers decline most of them. 7.3 fires when 7.2 says no. three offers arrive pre-set - bags pre-added (Q4Km), insurance pre-selected (MasT), paid seats pre-assigned (Q4Km) - so declining means finding the removal control first.

children.label: Choose the seats
children.note: 7.1.1 then 7.1.2 per flight; 7.1.3 instead where the seat is skipped or arrives pre-assigned.

questions.question: Do you want to pay an extra fee to select a specific seat, or skip seat selection to save money?
questions.why: The screen offers preferred and extra legroom seats for additional fees up to 41,760 NGN, so skipping this step avoids increasing the total fare.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to decide whether securing a specific seat is worth paying the additional fee.

questions.question: On the visual seat map, is the assigned seat a middle seat or located directly next to the lavatories?
questions.why: Seat numbers alone (like 28E) don't always clearly convey if it's a middle seat or in an undesirable location, which is immediately obvious to a sighted user looking at the graphical layout.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to avoid an uncomfortable middle seat or a noisy spot by the bathrooms because the agent only verified the seat number and price.

questions.question: Are there actually adjacent seats available for your group to sit together, or is the cabin mostly full?
questions.why: Even if you are willing to pay extra for seat selection, the seat map might reveal that no two seats are together, which is a dealbreaker for families traveling with children.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to abandon the booking for this specific flight before paying, avoiding a situation where your young child is forced to sit alone.

questions.question: Did the seat map actually assign you the seat you clicked, or did it throw an error saying the seat is no longer available?
questions.why: Seat maps can display stale inventory, and the seat you select might have been taken by another user moments before.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The agent might proceed thinking they secured a specific seat, when the system actually rejected the selection and left it unassigned.

questions.question: Do you want to confirm your choice to skip seat selection?
questions.why: The site displays a warning modal asking if you want to proceed because seats were not selected for all passengers.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide whether securing specific seats is important enough to go back and select them.

questions.question: Do you need to add checked baggage for an additional fee?
questions.why: Adding a 20 kg checked bag significantly increases the fare, as shown when the total jumped from 118 € to 218.10 €.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to decide whether your specific packing needs justify paying a steep baggage fee.

questions.question: Is the baggage summary correct, and is the current booking total acceptable before you move on to seat selection?
questions.why: The screen displays a baggage summary of ¥0 for both flights and a total of ¥21,270 JPY, which must be verified before adding other extras like seats.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the opportunity to personally ensure your specific luggage needs are accurately reflected in the price before proceeding.

questions.question: Are you sure you want to decline checked baggage now and risk paying higher fees at the airport?
questions.why: The warning modal explicitly shows that buying a 15 kg baggage allowance at the airport costs ¥4,600, compared to just ¥1,780 if purchased now.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to weigh your actual packing needs against the financial risk of paying a premium at the airport.

questions.question: Do you want to add Price Drop Protection to your search?
questions.why: The search screen includes an option to 'Add Price Drop Protection', where the platform will pay the difference if the price drops after booking.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to secure financial protection against future price drops before initiating the search.

questions.question: Do you want to add the flight protection plan before completing the booking?
questions.why: The screen requires you to explicitly choose whether to add or decline the $35.28 flight protection plan before the system will process the booking.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might make the wrong choice about purchasing travel insurance or fail the form submission entirely by skipping the required selection.

questions.question: Should you add any optional extras like Wi-Fi or a stopover package to your booking?
questions.why: The booking flow presents optional add-ons like in-flight Wi-Fi for 6,960 NGN or an Addis stopover package for 153,120 NGN that will increase your total fare.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might automatically skip these extras to minimize costs, depriving you of amenities you might prefer for a more comfortable journey.

questions.question: Do you want to go back to purchase add-ons now to save money, or proceed without them?
questions.why: The modal warns that add-on prices will increase if you wait to add them after booking.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the chance to decide whether to secure cheaper add-ons now or proceed without them.

children.label: Review and commit the booking
children.note: 8.1 with 8.2 against it. 8.3 whenever the platform moves the price mid-checkout - three keepers meet it, at three different spots, with three different outcomes. 8.4 and 8.5 as the screen asks - -dAg answers 8.4 before the passenger form even exists, and the choice changes the price. then 8.6; 8.7 and 8.8 only on the hold path (UiwB). no keeper pays money on camera.

questions.question: Has a session timeout warning appeared indicating you are about to lose your reserved fare and seats?
questions.why: Flight booking sessions usually have strict timers (e.g., 10-15 minutes) to hold inventory, and if the timer expires before payment is processed, you must restart and the price may jump.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the awareness that you need to immediately complete the payment or risk having the transaction fail and the fare disappear.

questions.question: Did the page reach a booking confirmation, or did the bank pop-up fail or time out?
questions.why: Airline payment processors often rely on 3D Secure pop-ups or bank redirects that can be blocked by browsers or time out, leaving the transaction in limbo.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the certainty of knowing whether your card was charged and your flight secured, potentially resulting in a lost reservation.

questions.question: Are you comfortable with the current booking total before adding bags?
questions.why: The screen shows a detailed breakdown of fares, fees, and taxes totaling ¥21,270 JPY that should be verified before proceeding to baggage selection.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to confirm the base fare and taxes align with their budget before extra add-on costs are introduced.

questions.question: Is the lowest fare actually offered higher than the price the calendar advertised?
questions.why: The date carousel advertised 672,720 NGN for May 14, but the lowest available fare class upon selection jumped to 730,269 NGN.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might blindly accept the higher fare without realizing the advertised price was misleading, causing you to overpay.

questions.question: Does the departure date match the airport arrival warning?
questions.why: The selected flight shows a departure on Tuesday, March 24, but the fare modal explicitly warns to arrive at the airport on Monday, March 25.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to catch a critical date discrepancy that could result in showing up at the airport on the wrong day.

questions.question: Do you accept the new, higher price to continue with the booking?
questions.why: The booking site alerted you that the ticket price increased to 149 € and asked if you want to accept the new fare or select an alternative trip.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: If an agent automatically accepts the price hike, you might end up paying more than you budgeted instead of exploring the cheaper alternatives provided.

questions.question: Do you accept the updated fare?
questions.why: The booking site displayed a notification that the fare decreased by ₹ 10 to ₹ 4,985, requiring you to acknowledge the new price before proceeding.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to personally review the dynamic price change and decide whether you still want to proceed with the transaction.

questions.question: Which payment method will you use, and are you willing to pay extra fees for certain options?
questions.why: The screen shows that selecting certain options like Payment Centers adds a PHP 224 hold fee to your booking total.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to decide whether the convenience of a specific payment method is worth the extra fee.

questions.question: Should you choose to be billed in the airline's local currency or accept the site's guaranteed exchange rate in your home currency?
questions.why: Booking sites and payment gateways often offer Dynamic Currency Conversion (DCC), which applies a heavily inflated exchange rate compared to letting your travel credit card handle the conversion.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might select your home currency thinking it is safer or clearer, inadvertently adding a 5-7% hidden markup to the final cost of the flight.

questions.question: Are you ready to commit to these non-refundable charges and proceed to payment?
questions.why: The prompt explicitly warns that proceeding locks in the fares and fees as non-cancellable charges, even if the browser is closed before paying.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the final opportunity to review or cancel the booking before being financially committed to the charges.

questions.question: Does this booking fall under a 24-hour risk-free cancellation policy?
questions.why: Many airlines and jurisdictions mandate a 24-hour grace period where even strictly non-refundable tickets can be canceled for a full refund.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the knowledge of exactly how long they have to safely reverse the transaction if they spot a mistake or their plans suddenly change right after booking.

questions.question: What hold code and expiry does the page show, and has anything been paid yet?
questions.why: The screen displays a banner confirming reservation OJGMQU is on hold and will expire in 23 hours and 59 minutes, which dictates your payment deadline.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you miss seeing the exact confirmation code and the specific deadline to pay before the held reservation expires.

questions.question: Does the final confirmation match the 24-hour payment window promised by the Book Now Pay Later option?
questions.why: Checking the expiration time on the final confirmation banner ensures you actually have the promised 24 hours to secure your fare.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the peace of mind of personally verifying the exact deadline to finalize your payment before the reservation expires.

questions.question: Does the confirmation page say the booking is ticketed, or only reserved until payment?
questions.why: The email explicitly states that the booking is not yet ticketed and provides specific options to complete your payment.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to personally review the emailed payment instructions and verify the exact ticketing status of your reservation.

questions.question: After booking, what does the confirmation page show?
questions.why: Checking the attached itinerary PDF confirms that the booking status is officially confirmed and the passenger details are accurate.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the immediate peace of mind of personally verifying the confirmed status and passenger details on the official itinerary receipt.

govbenefits.task: apply for a government benefit online or manage an existing claim (unemployment insurance, SNAP/food stamps, disability, Medicaid, housing assistance — state portals and agency sites): work through the eligibility screens and application form and submit, or certify/check an existing claim; complete when the submission confirmation or the claim-status screen is shown. Surface pinned: the government benefits portal itself — not benefit-explainer talking heads without a portal session.

tree.label: Claim a government benefit
tree.note: 1 then 2 every session. then the session's job: 3 once per claim, 4 every week the claim lives, 5 when certifying lapses, 8 once benefits flow onto the card. 6 closes 3, 4, and 5; 7 follows 6. the jobs chain across sessions - 3's confirmation starts the clock on 4, and 4 stays blocked while 5 processes (76Pa).

children.label: Reach the right program
children.note: 1.1 and 1.2 in either order; 1.3 and 1.4 before committing to the session - 1.4 can end it before it starts (iVa7's outage window). then 1.5. certifiers re-enter here every week.

questions.question: Before any credentials are entered, is this the official benefits portal for the agency named, rather than a lookalike?
questions.why: You must locate the correct button to access the Employment Development Department's online benefit services.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to verify that you are accessing the official state portal before handing over your credentials.

questions.question: Is this the official state government site for the benefits portal?
questions.why: Typing the exact URL in the address bar ensures you navigate directly to the official New York State Department of Labor portal.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to verify firsthand that your sensitive information is being submitted to the official government web address.

questions.question: Do you have a smartphone ready to take a picture of your ID and a selfie?
questions.why: The 'Before You Start' screen explicitly states that a smartphone is required to capture images of your ID and a selfie for identity verification.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An AI agent cannot physically use a smartphone to take a live selfie or photograph your physical ID card.

questions.question: Do you want to review the tips and document requirements before starting the application?
questions.why: The screen provides optional dropdowns with details on required documents and interview expectations that can help prepare you for the process.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to learn exactly what documents to gather beforehand and what to expect during the interview phase.

questions.question: Which method will you choose to file your claim given the online system's restricted hours?
questions.why: The screen lists online, phone, and mail options, but specifies that the online portal is only open during certain days and times.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to choose an alternative filing method like phone or mail if the online system is currently unavailable.

questions.question: Does the page show downtime or deadlines that could affect filing on time?
questions.why: The screen displays specific deadlines for weekly certifications and upcoming system downtime that could affect your ability to file on time.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you might miss critical information about system outages and strict deadlines for your weekly certification.

questions.question: Which service portal should you select?
questions.why: The screen offers distinct portals for individuals, businesses, and government entities, so you must choose the one that matches your account type.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to verify that the agent is accessing the correct portal for your personal Social Security record.

questions.question: Which benefit program portal should I access?
questions.why: The screen displays different benefit systems like UI Online, so you must select the one that matches your specific claim.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to ensure the agent is entering the correct portal for your specific type of benefit.

children.label: Establish the account
children.note: 2.1 decides the wall: sign in (2.4), register (2.2, sometimes on the agency, sometimes on Login.gov or ID.me - the evidence notes say which), or guest past a CAPTCHA (q2an; 8v-j allows guest for one program only). 2.3 where the agency demands proofing - D3uH and o9iF are entire sessions inside this goal, and CA and AZ interpose it mid-application (a0_z, 5P67).

questions.question: Did your account creation succeed, and are you now viewing the main dashboard?
questions.why: Confirming the 'my Social Security' dashboard loads ensures your account was created properly and displays your initial eligibility and work credits.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You miss seeing your immediate eligibility status, work credits summary, and any urgent unread messages upon first logging in.

questions.question: Did the portal block account creation because it detected that an active claim already exists for your Social Security Number?
questions.why: If someone else fraudulently used your SSN, or if you have an old forgotten account, the system will hard-stop the process.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent cannot resolve an SSN conflict, and you miss the immediate red flag that your identity may have been compromised.

questions.question: Do you want to log in, create an account, or apply without an account?
questions.why: The login page provides options to enter existing credentials, create a new profile, or use the link to apply without an account.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the choice of whether to link this application to a permanent account for easier tracking or to proceed immediately as a guest.

questions.question: Are you applying for a program other than SNAP that requires creating a new MyAccess account?
questions.why: The narrator clarifies that while a new account is optional for SNAP, it is strictly required if you are applying for any other program, even if you have an account in another portal.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might try to proceed as a guest for a non-SNAP program, which would violate the system's rules and prevent the application from being completed.

children.label: Register a new account
children.note: 2.2.1 then 2.2.2; 2.2.3 and 2.2.4 where the portal uses them; 2.2.5 where a confirmation email closes the loop; 2.2.6 wherever the form plants one. Or9Z fills everything and deliberately never submits - the narrator already has an account.

questions.question: Are you ready to submit this registration form?
questions.why: Clicking 'Next' officially submits the entered personal details to the government system to create a record.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to halt the process before a permanent, official government record is created with their personal data.

questions.question: Do you agree to the terms and conditions required to establish an online account?
questions.why: The screen states that you must check the agreement box and click 'I Agree' to accept the Terms and Conditions in order to create your EDD account.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to review the specific legal terms and conditions you are binding yourself to by creating the account.

questions.question: Do you meet the strict age and residency prerequisites required by the Terms of Service to create this account?
questions.why: The Terms of Service explicitly state you must have a U.S. mailing address and be at least 18 years of age to legally proceed with account creation.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to personally review the legal prerequisites and ensure they are not violating the Terms of Service by creating an account they are ineligible for.

questions.question: Can I use a shared email address for this account?
questions.why: The instructions explicitly state that you must use your own personal email address and not one shared with a spouse or family member.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means the agent might use a proxy email address, depriving you of direct, private access to critical communications regarding your benefits.

questions.question: Has the temporary PIN shown on screen been recorded before leaving the page?
questions.why: The screen explicitly instructs you to write down the temporary PIN before leaving, as it is required alongside your social security number for your initial login.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you will not know the temporary PIN required to access your newly registered account.

questions.question: Which personal image and caption should you select for your security check?
questions.why: The image and caption you choose will be displayed during future logins to confirm you are on the authentic EDD website before entering your password.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: If an agent selects these security features, you will not know the specific image and caption combination needed to verify the site's authenticity yourself.

questions.question: Confirming your email means opening your own inbox and clicking the link before it expires - do you take over that step?
questions.why: Clicking the 'Confirm email address' button in the Login.gov email is required to verify your address before the link expires in 24 hours.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step requires granting the agent access to your personal email inbox to click the confirmation link, which compromises your private communications.

questions.question: What characters do you need to enter from the CAPTCHA image?
questions.why: The 'Getting Started' page requires you to enter the exact text shown in the CAPTCHA image to verify you are human before proceeding.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means relying on the agent's ability to accurately read and solve visual CAPTCHAs, which often block automated systems.

children.label: Prove the identity
children.note: 2.3.1 first where a provider fork exists; then 2.3.2 and 2.3.3. one of 2.3.4 or 2.3.5 proves the person - documents and a selfie (D3uH), or typed details against credit records (o9iF), or a bare typed SSN (VNaP, 5P67 - CA and OH ask for nothing more than that plus a license number). 2.3.6 and 2.3.7 where the agency stacks its own layer on top.

questions.question: Are you ready to verify your identity using your driver's license and Social Security number?
questions.why: The screen explicitly states that a driver's license or state ID and your Social Security number are strictly required to prove your identity to the SSA.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step requires handing over highly sensitive physical identification documents and your Social Security number to a third-party agent.

questions.question: Which identity provider should you use to sign in or create your account?
questions.why: The portal requires choosing between third-party identity services like Login.gov or ID.me because the legacy Social Security username option is no longer available.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means you lose the opportunity to select the identity provider that best accommodates your specific residency status or existing account history.

questions.question: Was my account created before September 18, 2021, and should I use the legacy username login?
questions.why: The screen explicitly states that accounts created before this specific date must use the legacy Username and Password fields rather than the newer Login.gov or ID.me options.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might try to force a new Login.gov creation or use the wrong login path if it doesn't know the exact date the user originally created their account.

questions.question: Which multi-factor authentication method do you want to use?
questions.why: The portal requires setting up an additional layer of protection for your account and offers options like text messages, authenticator apps, or security keys.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this setup means the agent could link the authentication to its own phone or app, potentially locking you out of your government benefits account.

questions.question: Do you want to remember this browser when entering your one-time code?
questions.why: The screen includes a 'Remember this browser' checkbox that determines whether you will need to complete two-factor authentication on future logins from this device.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Letting an agent make this choice means losing personal control over the security and convenience settings for future access to your government benefits account.

questions.question: Do you authorize ID.me to share your verified identity information with the state agency?
questions.why: You must explicitly grant permission to share sensitive details like your SSN and date of birth with the state agency to continue your claim.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally review and consent to the exact pieces of sensitive information being transferred to the state agency.

questions.question: Does this window have to stay open while the ID photos are taken on the phone?
questions.why: The screen explicitly warns you not to close the window because it will automatically load the next step once the mobile verification is complete.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The agent cannot physically access your smartphone to take a picture of your ID, requiring you to step in and complete this out-of-band verification yourself.

questions.question: How do you complete the identity check on your phone?
questions.why: The screen displays an SMS from Login.gov containing both a one-time code and a document capture link, requiring a choice on how to complete the security check.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally handle the secure verification link and identity document capture sent directly to your mobile device.

questions.question: Do you need to unmask your Social Security number to verify it before submitting?
questions.why: The screen displays your Social Security number masked by default, providing a checkbox to reveal it so you can ensure it matches your records exactly before the system checks it.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to visually confirm your sensitive identifying number is typed correctly, which could cause verification failures and delay your benefits if there is a typo.

questions.question: How do you resolve the identity verification mismatch error?
questions.why: The portal blocks access until you resolve the identity mismatch by updating your personal information with the Social Security Administration or Login.gov.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent cannot resolve this identity mismatch because it requires updating your personal records directly with the Social Security Administration or Login.gov.

questions.question: What should you do if the activation code hasn't arrived?
questions.why: The screen warns that the code expires in 10 minutes, so you need to know how to use the "Having trouble?" dropdown if the text message is delayed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally troubleshoot or request an alternative verification method if the text message fails to reach your device.

questions.question: What is the activation code sent to my phone?
questions.why: The screen requires the activation code sent via text message to proceed, warning that it will expire in 10 minutes.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to directly receive and input the time-sensitive security code sent to their personal device.

questions.question: Has the personal key been captured and stored before the page's confirm button is pressed?
questions.why: If you forget your password and do not have this key, you will be forced to verify your identity all over again.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses direct possession of their account recovery key, making them reliant on the agent to securely store and provide it to them later.

questions.question: What is your password for this account?
questions.why: The login screen requires a password to authenticate your identity and grant access to your benefits account.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step requires sharing your highly sensitive government portal password with a third-party agent, which compromises your account's security.

questions.question: Do the displayed personal image and caption match what you set up?
questions.why: The screen requires you to verify your chosen image and caption to confirm the site's authenticity before entering your password.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally verify your unique security image and caption, which protects your password from being entered on a phishing site.

children.label: Apply for the benefit
children.note: 3.1 first - a Yes there can end the online path before it starts. 3.2 only on multi-program portals. 3.3 to 3.5 as the form asks; 3.6 per employer, repeated where the base period holds several. then 3.7; 3.8 where the state pays this way; 3.9 and 3.10 where offered, both skippable and both skipped. 6 closes it.

questions.question: Which sections of the application do I need to complete, and what is their current status?
questions.why: The application summary page lists all required categories like income, expenses, and assets, allowing you to track your progress and see what information is still needed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the high-level overview of the application's complexity and the specific categories of personal information that will be required.

questions.question: Do you want to submit an incomplete application immediately to secure your filing date?
questions.why: The popup explains that you have the right to file immediately with just your name, address, and signature to establish your application date, though it warns this might delay processing.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the strategic choice to secure an earlier benefit start date by submitting a minimal application today rather than waiting until they have all their information gathered.

questions.question: How should I answer the initial eligibility questions?
questions.why: These first five questions determine if you meet the basic legal requirements to proceed with the unemployment insurance application.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the ability to ensure your specific employment circumstances are accurately represented in the critical first eligibility check.

questions.question: Which benefit programs do you want to apply for?
questions.why: The 'Pick programs' screen requires you to select specific options like SNAP, TANF, or Health Care to determine the correct application path.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means the agent might select the wrong assistance program, potentially delaying or misdirecting your access to crucial benefits.

questions.question: Which health care category best describes your situation?
questions.why: The screen lists specific demographic categories like 'Pregnant women' or 'Adults caring for a child', and selecting the correct one determines your eligibility for Medicaid or CHIP.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means the agent might select a category that doesn't accurately reflect your life circumstances, potentially leading to an incorrect application or denial of benefits.

questions.question: Are you filling out this form for yourself or someone else?
questions.why: The form requires you to specify if you are applying for yourself and your household or on behalf of someone else.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally ensure the application correctly identifies whether it is for your own household or another individual.

questions.question: Do you want to designate an authorized representative to act on your behalf?
questions.why: This determines whether you want to grant another person the legal right to manage your benefits application and communicate with the agency for you.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The agent cannot know if you have a trusted individual you want to designate to handle your benefits or if you prefer to manage them yourself.

questions.question: Which address and contact details should I provide here?
questions.why: The screen requires your residence address, an optional mailing address, phone numbers, and email to ensure the agency can reach you about your claim.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose control over specifying your preferred contact methods, such as enabling text messages or choosing a separate mailing address.

questions.question: Do the name, address and contact details on this page match what you gave?
questions.why: Proceeding past this screen confirms that your contact and demographic details are accurate, which is essential for the agency to process your claim.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to personally spot-check your identifying details for typos or outdated information that could delay your benefits.

questions.question: What demographic information do you want to provide?
questions.why: The screen asks for personal details like race, ethnicity, gender, and disability status, which you may prefer not to answer.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the choice of whether to disclose or withhold sensitive demographic information.

questions.question: Are the default language settings correct, and do you need an interpreter?
questions.why: The screen asks for your preferred reading language and whether you need an interpreter, which dictates how the agency will communicate with you.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to specify a non-English language preference or request an interpreter for your case.

children.label: Report the work history
children.note: 3.6.1, then 3.6.2 and 3.6.3 per employer; 3.6.4 loops back into 3.6.1 for each further base-period employer (Or9Z adds one, then flips the gate answer to No). 3.6.5 wherever a free-typed occupation is refused; 3.6.6 where the claim doubles as a job-search profile. 5.4 is this goal's reopen twin, built on the state's wage records instead.

questions.question: Did you work for an employer within the last 18 months?
questions.why: Accurately reporting your employment history over the specified timeframe is required to determine your benefit eligibility.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means an agent might incorrectly report your recent work history, potentially resulting in a denied or delayed claim.

questions.question: Is my last employer's information completely accurate before I proceed?
questions.why: The screen displays a summary of your most recent employment details, which must be correct to prevent delays or denials in processing your claim.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally verify that your previous employment dates and employer contact details were entered correctly before advancing the application.

questions.question: Are your employment details, specifically the reason for separation, correct?
questions.why: The screen requires selecting a reason for separation, such as 'Laid Off' or 'Discharge/Fired', which directly determines your eligibility for unemployment benefits.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means losing the ability to accurately report why your employment ended, risking a denied claim or penalties if the wrong reason is selected.

questions.question: How do you calculate your gross wages for each past quarter if you don't have exact pay stubs?
questions.why: The form requires you to enter gross wages for six specific past quarters, which directly impacts your benefit calculation.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to ensure the estimated quarterly wages accurately reflect your actual past work hours and pay rate.

questions.question: Are the gross wages you entered consistent with your last day worked?
questions.why: Entering a full quarter's worth of wages contradicts your earlier entry showing your last day worked was weeks before the quarter ended, which could trigger a fraud flag or delay your claim.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to ensure your reported income mathematically aligns with your actual employment dates to prevent your application from being rejected or audited.

questions.question: Did you work for any other employers during the specified timeframe?
questions.why: The application requires you to declare all employment between specific dates to accurately determine your benefit eligibility.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might not know your complete work history for those exact dates, risking an incomplete application or a penalty for omitting a past employer.

questions.question: Is the second employment-history question actually required?
questions.why: Skipping fields on the employment history page might lead to an incomplete application or a denial of benefits if that information is required.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to decide whether omitting specific employment details might negatively impact your benefit eligibility.

questions.question: How do you find and select the correct occupation codes for your job profile?
questions.why: Using the 'Occupation Lookup' button ensures your work history is accurately categorized with the standard codes required for the application.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally search the lookup tool to ensure the selected occupation code perfectly matches your specific job duties.

questions.question: How many occupations does the page say to give, and how many does it require?
questions.why: The page instructions say to select 'up to 2 occupations', but both occupation fields have asterisks indicating they are mandatory.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might arbitrarily select a second occupation just to satisfy the form validation, potentially misrepresenting your actual job search preferences.

questions.question: How many months of experience and which specific skills should you list for your selected occupations?
questions.why: The screen requires you to input your months of experience for two specific occupation codes and describe the skills that qualify you for those roles.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might guess your experience level or list generic skills that do not accurately reflect your actual work history and qualifications.

questions.question: What is the lowest acceptable hourly wage and shift schedule you will declare you are willing to work?
questions.why: The state uses your minimum acceptable wage and shift availability to determine if you are genuinely available for work; setting the wage too high or restricting shifts can automatically disqualify you from receiving benefits.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might guess a minimum wage or shift preference that either disqualifies you for being too restrictive or legally commits you to accepting jobs you cannot actually take.

questions.question: How do you answer the eligibility questions about other income, recall dates, and school or union status?
questions.why: The screen requires details on pensions, severance pay, and recall dates, which directly determine your eligibility and benefit amount.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally verify that your specific financial details and employment status are reported accurately.

questions.question: Has the page flagged any availability questions as still unanswered?
questions.why: Skipping required fields on the Availability Information page will trigger an error and prevent you from advancing to the next step.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to accurately report their specific work availability, which is critical for determining their benefit eligibility.

children.label: Choose how benefits arrive
children.note: 3.8.1, with 3.8.2 read where the card is chosen or is the default; 3.8.3 and 3.8.4 where the form offers them. applications only - certifications touch withholding through 4.7, and D3uH sets 3.8.4 from inside account setup.

questions.question: How would you like to receive your benefit payments?
questions.why: The portal requires you to choose between receiving your funds via direct deposit to a bank account or automatically receiving a prepaid debit card.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Letting an agent decide means you lose control over the specific financial account or method used to access your benefit funds.

questions.question: Did the system reject your bank's routing number, forcing you to either provide a different account or accept a fee-heavy prepaid debit card?
questions.why: Legacy state systems frequently reject routing numbers from smaller credit unions or newer online banks, which can automatically default your payment method to a state-issued debit card.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to provide an alternative bank account, potentially getting locked into a prepaid card that charges ATM and maintenance fees.

questions.question: Are you comfortable with the fees and terms associated with the debit card payment option?
questions.why: The screen displays the U.S. Bank ReliaCard fee disclosure, detailing potential costs like out-of-network ATM and inactivity fees that will affect your benefit funds.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to personally evaluate the debit card's fee structure and decide if another payment method might save you money.

questions.question: Do you want federal and state taxes withheld from your benefit payments?
questions.why: This determines whether taxes are deducted directly from your benefits, which affects both your immediate payout amount and your end-of-year tax liability.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Letting an agent make this choice means losing control over your personal tax strategy and the net amount of your immediate benefit payments.

questions.question: Did the screen confirm the notice preferences were saved before continuing back to the account home page?
questions.why: The screen confirms your preferences were successfully updated and provides a button to continue to your my Social Security homepage.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the immediate visual confirmation that your account preferences were saved correctly before entering the main portal.

questions.question: How do you want to receive notices from Social Security?
questions.why: You must choose whether to receive only secure online notices or both paper and online notices before saving and continuing.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose the ability to decide whether you receive important physical mail or only digital communications from Social Security.

questions.question: Do you want to backdate this claim, and if so, to what date and for what reason?
questions.why: The system requires a specific effective date and a written explanation if you choose to backdate your unemployment claim.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to provide their specific personal justification for the delayed filing, which is required to process the backdate request.

questions.question: Did the application let you proceed to the next screen without filling in the required reason for backdating?
questions.why: The system advanced to the Employer screen even though the field marked with an asterisk for backdating the claim was left blank.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to ensure their application is fully complete, risking a delay or denial if the agency later flags the missing explanation.

questions.question: Which of the suggested documents do you want to upload now?
questions.why: The screen lists suggested documents like proof of income that you can upload now, though it notes you can still submit the application without them.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to decide whether to gather and provide these documents immediately or wait for the eligibility worker to require them.

questions.question: Did the system reject your document upload due to a file size or format error, allowing you to proceed but guaranteeing a manual review delay?
questions.why: State portals often have archaic file constraints (e.g., 2MB PDF only). If an upload fails, the system may still let you click 'Next', but your claim will be delayed for missing evidence.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the awareness that their critical proof of income or ID was never actually attached, leading to a surprise denial or weeks of delay.

children.label: Certify a claim week
children.note: 4.1, then 4.2 and 4.3 as the portal interposes them. 4.4, with 4.5 where a No on earnings spawns it; 4.6 as the state requires. repeat 4.4 to 4.6 once per claim week in the session - lVpW and urAf each run two. 4.7 rides on the final week only. 6 closes it.

questions.question: Are there weeks available to certify for benefits, and what is the deadline?
questions.why: The dashboard notification indicates you have weeks available to certify and warns that missing the specified deadline could affect your eligibility.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose direct visibility into your current claim balance and the exact deadline required to keep your benefits active.

questions.question: Should you read the detailed eligibility text before clicking the 'Certify for Benefits' button?
questions.why: The screen displays detailed eligibility information below the notification box that could contain important requirements or updates for your claim.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally review the specific eligibility criteria presented on the screen before initiating the certification process.

questions.question: What fraud rules must I acknowledge to proceed?
questions.why: You must check the box to confirm you understand the penalties for fraud, such as failing to report new earnings, before you can continue.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to personally review the specific legal obligations and fraud penalties you are being held accountable for.

questions.question: Should you read the payment processing details before clicking continue?
questions.why: The page contains important details about direct deposit and processing times, such as a five-day wait, that affect how and when you receive your benefits.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to understand the timeline for receiving your funds and the rules for updating your banking information.

questions.question: Is your contact information correct, or do you need to update it?
questions.why: The screen explicitly warns that you must keep your contact information current, requiring you to verify the displayed address, phone, and email before continuing.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to verify that the agency has your most up-to-date address and phone number for critical benefit communications.

questions.question: How should I answer the weekly certification questions about my availability, work search, and earnings?
questions.why: Accurately answering these specific questions about sickness, work search, and earnings is required to determine your continued eligibility for weekly benefits.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means the agent might incorrectly report your personal work search efforts or earnings for the week, potentially risking your benefits or triggering fraud flags.

questions.question: Are the pre-filled answers to the weekly eligibility questions correct for your situation?
questions.why: You must verify that the answers regarding whether you worked, refused work, or received a pension during the specified week are accurate before proceeding.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to personally verify your weekly activities and income, risking an inaccurate claim being submitted on your behalf.

children.label: Prove the work search
children.note: the state sets the shape: 4.6.1 where the rules need reading; repeat 4.6.2 until the quota holds (iVa7 needs three that count, 2mL- three when the activities are applications); 4.6.3 where the log arrives pre-filled; 4.6.4 where the page invites its own bypassing. absent entirely for some claim types - Jt5q answers a question instead, and xoKC has no log step yet certifies work-search activities at 6.4.

questions.question: Do you need to add more job contacts to meet the weekly minimum?
questions.why: The screen warns that you must report at least three job contacts per week or your unemployment benefit payment may be denied.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the ability to accurately report your specific job search efforts to ensure your benefits are approved.

questions.question: Do you need to review the help text to understand what qualifies as looking for work?
questions.why: The 'UI Online Help' window provides specific definitions for what counts as looking for work, ensuring you answer the eligibility question accurately.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to personally review the agency's specific definitions to ensure your recent activities actually qualify.

questions.question: What are the application details for this job contact?
questions.why: The screen requires you to specify your interest level, whether you contacted the employer, the date, and the contact method to log your work search activity.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to accurately report the specific dates and methods of your personal job search efforts.

questions.question: Are your logged work search methods valid despite the warning to only use the Reemployment Exchange?
questions.why: An on-screen caption explicitly requires using the Reemployment Exchange, but the system's log shows that 'In Person' and 'EMail' contacts were accepted.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to clarify if their alternative work search methods will ultimately be rejected and cause a claim denial despite appearing accepted in the log.

questions.question: Do you need to provide work search details for this week?
questions.why: The screen provides an option to bypass the work search entry by clicking 'Next', which is important to notice if your specific employment status exempts you from this requirement.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means an agent might incorrectly skip or fabricate work search records without knowing your actual exemption status or weekly activities.

questions.question: Do you want to withhold taxes from this week's payment or update your contact information?
questions.why: The weekly certification form includes optional questions asking if you want federal taxes withheld from your payment or if you need to update your mailing address.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose direct control over your tax withholding preferences and the opportunity to ensure your contact details are current.

children.label: Reopen the claim
children.note: 5.1 - an expired claim exits to a new application through 3, and employer-issued claim forms exit to the phone. then 5.2, 5.3, 5.4; 6 closes it. 4 stays blocked until the request processes.

children.label: Read the claim status and choose the path

questions.question: Do I need to reopen my claim based on my current notifications?
questions.why: The screen shows a notification that you haven't certified recently and must click the button to reopen your claim.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you miss seeing the specific reason your claim was paused and the special instructions regarding employer or union claim forms.

questions.question: Has your claim expired, requiring you to file a new claim instead of reopening the old one?
questions.why: The dashboard notification explicitly states the claim has expired, which changes the required action from simply certifying or reopening to filing a completely new claim.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might try to certify for weeks on an expired claim, wasting time or causing confusion, instead of realizing a new application is required.

questions.question: How should you answer the eligibility questions regarding other income and specific employment situations?
questions.why: The application requires you to declare any expected Workers' Compensation or other employer income and clarify if your unemployment is due to a trade dispute to determine your benefit eligibility.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means the agent might incorrectly report your other income sources or mischaracterize the exact reason for your unemployment, potentially jeopardizing your claim.

questions.question: Should you save your application as a draft to finish later?
questions.why: The narrator explains that clicking the 'Save as Draft' button preserves your progress until Saturday at 11:59 pm PST if you need to step away to gather more information.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide when to pause the application and the awareness of the strict Saturday deadline to resume before your data is deleted.

children.label: Identify the last employer from the records

questions.question: Which employer from the provided list should I select as my last employer?
questions.why: The agency requires you to accurately identify the very last employer you performed work for, regardless of whether the job was full-time, part-time, or temporary.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to ensure the exact final employer is selected, which is critical if you recently juggled multiple temporary or part-time jobs that an agent might confuse.

questions.question: What is your last employer's state ID number?
questions.why: The system requires the 8-digit state ID number from box 15 of your W-2 to search for and link your last employer to your claim.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to directly provide the exact state ID number from your personal W-2, which ensures the correct employer is linked to your claim.

children.label: Attest and submit
children.note: 6.1 with 6.2 against it, then 6.3, 6.4, 6.5 - the states vary the signature, never the order. entered from 3, 4, or 5. five keepers stop at or inside this goal: Or9Z, a0_z, and urAf end before 6.5, q2an never reaches it, and 802J presses it with the result unshown.

questions.question: Are your claim summary answers correct, and do you agree to the legal certification terms under penalty of perjury?
questions.why: This matters because the screen requires you to review your eligibility and income summaries and legally certify that the information is correct.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to personally verify the accuracy of your claim details before legally binding yourself to the certification terms.

questions.question: Are you ready to proceed to the final review and submit section?
questions.why: The screen indicates you have completed the previous sections and offers the choice to save and exit or start the final review.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to decide whether to pause your application or proceed immediately to the final review.

questions.question: How do you safely return to a previous section to fix a mistake you spotted on the summary page?
questions.why: If you find an error in your previous answers, you must find the portal's internal 'Edit' buttons rather than using the browser's back button, which often clears the entire form.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to safely correct their own earlier mistake without risking the destruction of their current session state.

children.label: Check the answers against the earlier screens

questions.question: Do the gross wages and hours on the summary match what you earned?
questions.why: The summary page displays $100.00 in gross wages for 10 hours worked, and verifying this implied $10.00 hourly rate ensures your benefits are calculated correctly.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means losing the opportunity to catch data-entry errors in your reported wages or hours that could result in claim denial or overpayment penalties.

questions.question: Does the summary table include all the job contacts you listed on the previous screen?
questions.why: The summary table dropped the 'Salad Chef' job contact that was just listed, meaning your work search record is now incomplete.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to catch a system error that omitted one of your job contacts, which could jeopardize your weekly benefit payment.

questions.question: Are there any fields on the review screen highlighted in red indicating a silent validation error?
questions.why: Sometimes submitting a form fails silently, simply returning to the review screen with the problematic fields outlined in red without a prominent error message at the top.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: If the agent just says the page reloaded, the user won't know that a visual-only validation error is blocking the submission.

children.label: Verify and track the claim
children.note: 7.1 then 7.2 before leaving the page - one receipt is unrecoverable once closed (76Pa). 7.3 with 7.4 against it; 7.5 where messages sit unread; 7.6 to leave. 7.3 and 7.4 also open later sessions - certifiers read the same dashboard on the way in at 4.1.

children.label: Read the confirmation and next steps

questions.question: Did my submission go through, and what's my confirmation number?
questions.why: The success message confirms your certification was received, and the confirmation number provides essential proof in case of future payment delays.
