questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally verify that the correct file or Drive link is selected and attached to the message.

questions.question: Did the screenshot save to your desktop?
questions.why: Waiting for the file 'Screenshot [number] at 23.15.04.png' to appear on the Mac desktop confirmed that the image was successfully captured and saved.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the certainty of visually verifying that a local record of the commitment was actually created and saved to their machine.

questions.question: Which file do you want to attach to the message?
questions.why: The screen displays a file picker with multiple recent images and documents, requiring a choice of which specific file to attach.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to handpick the exact file, such as a transaction receipt, that supports their commitment.

questions.question: Has your attachment finished uploading?
questions.why: Waiting for the blue progress bar on the attachment chip to disappear ensures the file is fully attached before you click send.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the peace of mind that their required file was successfully included with the message rather than being dropped by a premature send.

questions.question: Is the attached file the one you meant to send?
questions.why: The draft screen shows an attached PDF file named 'Naveen Demo.pdf' with an 'X' button next to it for removal.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to catch and remove an incorrect file before committing to the message.

questions.question: Is the file over the size limit, so it would go as a link instead of a copy?
questions.why: The screen showed a dialog stating the files exceed the 25 MB limit and will automatically be converted to Google Drive links.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the chance to cancel the upload and choose an alternative way to share or compress the large files.

children.label: Set the message terms
children.note: 6.1 first, then one of 6.2 to 6.6 as the feature demands: 6.2 in vmDl, 6.3 and 6.4 in xjBI, 6.5 and 6.6 in NKK1. 6.8 sits beside 6.2 on the same ribbon and no keeper takes it. 6.7 after any of them - and after 4.9.8.4, where the poll card is the proof.

questions.question: Should you add voting buttons to this message?
questions.why: The Options tab reveals a 'Use Voting Buttons' feature that allows you to collect structured responses from the recipient.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide if a formal polling mechanism is the best way to handle the recipient's response to your commitment.

questions.question: Should you enable confidential mode for this email?
questions.why: The compose window displays a lock icon and a banner suggesting confidential mode to help keep your information safe.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means losing the ability to decide whether the sensitive nature of your commitment requires extra security restrictions.

questions.question: Which options do you want people to vote on?
questions.why: The screen showed preset options like 'Yes;No' and 'Approve;Reject', but selecting 'Custom...' was necessary to create choices suitable for a lunch vote.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to tailor the response options to the specific context and needs of their message.

questions.question: Do you want to change the expiry or passcode on this confidential email?
questions.why: The default settings expire the email in one week without an SMS passcode, which might not fit the security or timeframe needed for your commitment.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means the agent might accept the default one-week expiry, potentially causing the recipient to lose access to your message too soon.

questions.question: Should this follow-up flag apply to you or the recipient?
questions.why: The custom dialog box requires choosing whether the flag and reminder are set for your own inbox or the recipient's.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might set the flag for the wrong person, failing to prompt the recipient or unnecessarily adding a reminder to your own task list.

questions.question: What do you want to ask the recipient to do?
questions.why: The screen shows the 'Custom' flag dialog with the 'Flag for Recipients' option checked and the 'Flag to:' combo box displaying 'Follow up'.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to explicitly signal the expected action to the recipient using the email client's built-in flagging features.

questions.question: Is the reminder box checked, and for when?
questions.why: The screen shows an unchecked 'Reminder:' box with a default date and time, offering a built-in way to track the obligation.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to decide exactly when they need to be reminded to fulfill the obligation they are creating.

questions.question: Do the voting options on the message match the ones you asked for?
questions.why: The information bar and the checked item in the 'Use Voting Buttons' dropdown confirmed that the specific choices 'Thai;American;Italian' would be sent to recipients.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the certainty of visually confirming the exact voting options recipients will receive before the email goes out.

questions.question: Is the scheduling poll in the message body?
questions.why: The side panel confirms the poll is ready to be shared, and the email body displays the poll block with the correct duration and time options.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The delegator loses the ability to visually verify that the poll details are accurate and properly embedded before sending the message.

children.label: Review and send the message
children.note: 7.1 to 7.3 as the keeper bothers - EBqe runs all three, most run none and go straight to 7.4. 7.5 instead of 7.4 where the send is a question (3qL6, gBs-, 7V6o, vmDl). 7.6 replaces 7.4 in uQjR and is passed over in s3Um and ixyD. 7.7 once per page in zZ3x. 7.8 after any send that shows a toast. A refused send goes to 2.6.

questions.question: With the recipient list expanded, are the recipients exactly the people you picked?
questions.why: The screen showed a new message window with multiple recipients already populated, making the subject field the next logical step.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to visually verify that the correct recipients are included before committing to the draft.

questions.question: Do you want to send a message that's only a link, with no words?
questions.why: The screen shows a message containing just a bare link, which might lack necessary context or professionalism.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to decide whether to add context or a polite greeting to a bare link before committing to sending it.

questions.question: Did the event save with the guests and details you asked for?
questions.why: The pop-up details card displayed the meeting time, guest list, and description, confirming the commitment was accurately recorded.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the immediate reassurance of visually confirming that their meeting invitation was successfully created with the correct participants.

questions.question: Is the new project made and open on its talent pool?
questions.why: The screen shows the newly created project in the dashboard and its details page with the 'Talent pool' tab.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the assurance that the project was correctly set up to organize the candidates they intend to message.

questions.question: Are you ready to click 'Send'?
questions.why: Clicking this button dispatches the message and triggers the 'Message sent' confirmation, making your commitment official.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the final moment of control to halt the dispatch before the obligation becomes irreversible.

questions.question: After pressing Send, did a sent confirmation appear?
questions.why: The video promises to show how to send a connection request but ends while the cursor is hovering over the 'Send' button, never showing the result.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The agent loses the critical final steps of executing the send action and verifying its success.

questions.question: What access should the recipients get to the attached files?
questions.why: The screen presented a modal asking whether to allow anyone with the link to view the attached files or to send without giving access.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means losing the ability to control the specific privacy and sharing permissions for the attached files.

questions.question: Do you want to email the new guest an invite?
questions.why: The screen showed a modal dialog asking whether to send invitation emails to Google Calendar guests.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the choice of whether to explicitly notify the guest via an automated email or add the event silently.

questions.question: Send it now, or schedule it for later?
questions.why: The screen showed a dropdown arrow next to the 'Send' button, offering a choice between immediate dispatch and delayed delivery.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to strategically time when the recipient receives the commitment.

questions.question: Is the send time it suggests OK?
questions.why: The dialog presents a default send time of tomorrow at 8:00 AM Philippine Standard Time, which may not be when you actually want the recipient to get the message.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose control over the exact delivery time of your commitment, risking the message arriving at an inappropriate or ineffective hour if the agent simply accepts the default.

questions.question: Did it send, and is the undo still on screen?
questions.why: The screen displayed a 'Message sent' toast with options to 'Undo' or 'View message', confirming the send action.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the brief opportunity to immediately undo the sent message if they realize a mistake.

children.label: Confirm the message went
children.note: 8.1 or 8.2 on the sending side; 8.3 where the toast said Sent and the inbox says otherwise - kvML alone, and it looks past it. 8.4 to 8.6 where the keeper crosses to the recipient's side, eight of 24. 8.7 for the corpus's one round trip.

questions.question: Is the message in Sent yet, or still in the Outbox?
questions.why: The Gmail sidebar menu contains an 'Outbox' label where messages with heavy files are temporarily held until they finish sending.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the reassurance of manually checking the Outbox to confirm whether a delayed message is still in transit.

questions.question: Is the message in the Scheduled folder, or did it go out or stay a draft?
questions.why: Opening the folder list to check the Scheduled folder confirms that the app properly registered your future commitment.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the visual confirmation that your message is safely queued to be sent at the correct time.

questions.question: Does the sent forward include the original message under your note?
questions.why: The screen showed a collapsed forwarded message with a '> Show original message' link, requiring you to expand it to verify the full text.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The delegator loses the assurance that the forwarded content was correctly included and formatted in the final sent message.

questions.question: Has a bounce come back saying the message didn't get through?
questions.why: The top email in the inbox showed an 'Address not found' snippet, meaning the message did not reach the recipient.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user falsely believes their commitment was communicated, leaving the recipient unaware.

children.label: Handle the responses
children.note: 9.1 for the sender's own vote, 9.2 for the others; then 9.3 and 9.4 as the tally comes in. 9.5 when the poll decides a meeting. 9.6 on the invite link. 9.7 on the recruiting side. 9.8 where the corpus fails and shows no repair. 9.9 last, in one keeper.

questions.question: Which option is selected in your own vote, and is it sending now?
questions.why: The screen displays a voting dropdown with cuisine options and a dialog asking whether to send the response immediately or edit it first.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to select their preferred choice and decide whether to add additional context before the vote is sent.

questions.question: What's the tally, and who hasn't voted?
questions.why: The Message Tracking window displayed the reply totals and individual responses, which dictates the outcome you are committing to in the message.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to personally review the voting breakdown and ensure the correct choice is made based on the group's preferences.

questions.question: Book the meeting on the votes so far, or wait for everyone?
questions.why: The screen shows that required attendees like Bill Lumbergh haven't responded yet, and the preferred 2:30 PM slot already has one 'No' vote.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The delegator loses the nuanced human judgment of weighing strong preferences against outright rejections and knowing when to wait for crucial stakeholders before committing.

questions.question: Does the event page match the invite's date and time?
questions.why: Checking the event landing page ensures the recipient will see the correct date, time, and functional Yes, No, or Maybe buttons.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the peace of mind that comes from manually verifying the recipient's exact view of the event details and RSVP options.

questions.question: What status should the candidate get now that you've messaged them?
questions.why: The screen shows a "Change status" dropdown with options like "Contacted" and "Screened" to track the candidate's progress.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to define their own workflow rules for categorizing candidates in the pipeline.

questions.question: What should go in the candidate's notes?
questions.why: The screen shows a 'Note' icon and existing notes, indicating this is the designated place to maintain context about the candidate.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The delegator loses the assurance that nuanced insights, such as salary expectations or contact preferences, are captured for future interactions.

questions.question: What does the send error say?
questions.why: The screen displays an error state in the chat window that must be cleared using the 'X' button so you can return to the main interface and resolve the issue.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to personally read the error details and understand what caused the failure before the alert is dismissed.

news.task: find the latest news about a specific topic (a company, a person, a sport, a technology) on a news site or aggregator (google news, apnews, reuters, bbc, espn): search for or navigate to the topic, sort by or judge recency, and open the relevant latest article; complete when a current article on the right topic is on screen. Surface pinned: news sites and aggregators. Variants: news commentary/opinion videos as the subject, and "daily news recap" videos where a person reads headlines to camera, do not belong.

tree.label: Keep up with the news
tree.note: do 1. 2 and 3 feed each other and repeat - the Feedly keepers build with 2 and then scan what accrues with 3; the Google keepers run 3 alone and keep nothing (RKSc, gyDs, xATD, vLA0), except one topic follow that reaches into 2.6 (64Vu). 4 from any list, though most lists are scanned and left - 9 stories and one video clip get opened across 14 keepers. 5 after 4 where the story is worth keeping; 4_Sv runs 5 without ever opening the story. 6 replaces 4 and 5 on the newsroom service (AE9a). 7 in the one keeper that closes the loop (v4vm).

questions.question: Does the sidebar already list a feed that covers the asked topic?
questions.why: The sidebar displays existing categories like 'Marketing' alongside a '+' icon to 'Follow New Sources', requiring a choice between current and new content streams.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally curate which specific news publications are added to your account.

children.label: Get into the news service
children.note: 1.1 or 1.2 to arrive. 1.3 to 1.5 only where an account gates the service - three Feedly keepers start mid-session and skip all of it (4_Sv, zCA3, r9X3), and every Google keeper walks in without an account. 1.6 replaces 1.4 on the newsroom service (AE9a). 1.7 where the edition matters (gyDs).

questions.question: Does the pre-loaded search on the page match the topic you asked for?
questions.why: The screen shows the Google News Timeline labs page pre-loaded with a search for 'christmas' and dates from December 2009.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to define the specific starting platform, search term, and historical timeframe for the task.

questions.question: Which search result is the official Feedly website?
questions.why: The first search result displays the URL 'https://feedly.com/', confirming it is the legitimate aggregator rather than a third-party or sponsored link.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally verify the search result URL to ensure you are accessing the authentic news platform.

children.label: Choose log in or sign up

questions.question: Do you want to log in to an existing account or create a new one?
questions.why: The homepage displays both 'GET STARTED FOR FREE' and 'LOGIN' buttons, requiring a choice based on whether you already have an account.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to ensure the agent uses your existing account with its pre-configured news feeds rather than starting from scratch.

questions.question: Does the page offer an OPML import option?
questions.why: The screen presents options to either start a new free account or import an existing OPML file to set up your news feeds.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means the agent might create a new blank account instead of importing your existing curated news feeds.

questions.question: Which authentication method do you want to use to log in?
questions.why: The login modal presents multiple options like Google, Feedly, and various social accounts, requiring you to choose the one linked to your existing profile.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses control over which personal or third-party account is used to authenticate and access their personalized news feeds.

questions.question: Which Google account should you use to sign in to Feedly?
questions.why: The screen presents multiple Google accounts to continue to Feedly, and the choice determines which personalized news feed and subscriptions are accessed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to control which specific personal or work profile is associated with your news reading activity.

questions.question: Does the sign-in form show a pre-filled username to sign in with?
questions.why: The screen displays a login panel with a pre-filled username and obscured password, requiring a decision on whether to proceed and if the session should be saved.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to manage their own login credentials and decide whether the session should be persistently saved on the device.

questions.question: What language and region does the page say the feed is set to?
questions.why: The sidebar currently displays 'English (Nigeria)', which will heavily influence the geographic focus and relevance of the news results you receive.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to specify the exact cultural and geographic context that determines which local or regional news stories are prioritized.

children.label: Build the source feed
children.note: 2.1, then 2.2 or 2.3 raises candidates; 2.4 on every card, 2.5 where a sneak peek is wanted. 2.6 commits and 2.7 follows immediately - the platform will not let a follow float unfiled (2o_3); 64Vu's topic star is the exception, a follow with no filing step. 2.8 inside 2.7 when the feed is new; v4vm also runs 2.8 standalone and fills the empty feed afterward. repeat 2.2 to 2.7 per source - four in about 15 seconds (zCA3), six in a sitting (1HW8). 2.9 after any batch; 2.10 wherever the counts are on screen.

children.label: Search for a topic or source

questions.question: What is the results-language filter set to?
questions.why: The screen shows a 'Results language' dropdown with multiple options, allowing you to filter the news articles by languages like English, Spanish, or Japanese.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to specify your preferred reading language or to intentionally seek out foreign-language coverage of the topic.

questions.question: What specific blog or source do you want to search for?
questions.why: The search bar requires you to input the exact name of the publication or topic you want to read about.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally select a trusted, niche source that aligns with your specific professional interests.

questions.question: Which listed category matches the asked topic?
questions.why: The screen displays various featured industries and skills, making it necessary to choose the right category to surface relevant news sources.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means losing the opportunity to browse and select a specific niche topic that perfectly aligns with your current interests.

questions.question: Which video channel in the sidebar matches the asked topic?
questions.why: The left sidebar lists multiple regional and topical video channels under Broadcast Video, requiring a choice to narrow down the news content.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means losing the ability to prioritize which specific region's news is most relevant to your current interests.

questions.question: Which source should you select from the matching results?
questions.why: The screen displayed multiple matching sources with varying follower counts and posting frequencies, requiring a subjective choice.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to apply their personal taste or specific niche interest when choosing among multiple valid sources.

questions.question: Do the recent article titles in the preview match the asked topic?
questions.why: Scanning the article titles grouped under 'TODAY' and 'YESTERDAY' helps you verify if the source consistently publishes content that matches your target topic.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally evaluate the nuance and quality of the article titles to decide if the source truly aligns with your specific interests.

questions.question: Does the page show a follow control for this source?
questions.why: Clicking the star icon changes the status to 'Following' and triggers a confirmation toast, altering your account's saved preferences.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses control over the curation of their personalized news feed if the agent autonomously follows topics.

questions.question: Does the follow dropdown offer an existing feed that matches the topic?
questions.why: The dropdown menu after clicking follow requires choosing whether to organize this source into an existing category like 'Journalism' or to create a brand new feed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally organize your news sources into custom categories that match your specific reading habits.

questions.question: Does the modal show the intended feed title and collection?
questions.why: The modal displays the feed title and the selected collection, requiring verification before saving.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to verify and choose exactly which custom collection the topic feed is saved into.

questions.question: Does the page ask for a name for the new feed?
questions.why: The screen provides an input field and suggestions like '+ Black women', requiring a decision on how to label the topic.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means losing the ability to organize and name your news sources according to your own personal categories.

questions.question: Does the new feed appear in the sidebar?
questions.why: The sidebar updated to show 'EdTech' and 'MindShift' under 'FEEDS', confirming the topic was added and providing a way to access its articles.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to confirm the feed was added successfully and to choose exactly which source to view.

questions.question: Does the feed's unread count update correctly when you add new sources?
questions.why: Seeing the unread count immediately jump to 20 confirms that the platform successfully pulled in the latest articles from the sources you just added.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the immediate visual reassurance that your custom feed is correctly aggregating the specific sources you care about.

children.label: Check the counts against the earlier screens

questions.question: Does each feed's unread state match the article dates shown inside it?
questions.why: The screen shows the 'Black Women in History' feed claiming you are caught up despite containing an article from yesterday, while the 'Journalism' feed immediately displays accurate unread counts.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might trust the false 'caught up' message and fail to find the latest news, whereas a human would manually check the feed to verify.

questions.question: Does the publication frequency shown on the feed header agree with the search result?
questions.why: The feed header for MindShift states it publishes one article per month, contradicting the search result which claimed four articles per week.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might miss this contradiction and rely on inaccurate search results regarding how often the source publishes.

children.label: Pull up the stories
children.note: 3.1 or 3.2 or 3.3 raises a list - the Google keepers pull per section or query and keep nothing, the Feedly keepers open what 2 built. 3.4 only where the surface offers filters, and vLA0 round-trips every one before a single range sticks. 3.5 on every list; 3.6 where the surface clusters outlets; 3.7 on the newsroom service. re-entered per query - three searches in a row (64Vu).

questions.question: Does the page offer mute filters?
questions.why: The screen offers a 'GET MUTE FILTERS' button designed to remove irrelevant articles and fine-tune the news feed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to permanently customize their feed by filtering out specific unwanted keywords.

questions.question: Which sidebar tab is active, the algorithmic For-you or the followed one?
questions.why: The left sidebar displays distinct navigation options like 'For you' and 'Following', which dictate whether you see algorithmically suggested news or topics you have explicitly chosen.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to leverage your personally curated feeds to quickly locate topics you already track.

questions.question: What topics, locations, and sources are you currently following?
questions.why: Reviewing the empty state messages under the 'Topics & Sources' tab confirms whether you have already set up quick access to the specific subject you want to read about.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the awareness of your account's current personalization state and the knowledge that no specific topics or sources are currently saved for quick access.

questions.question: Which sidebar feed matches the asked topic?
questions.why: The expanded sidebar shows multiple marketing sources with unread counts, requiring a choice of which specific publication or author to prioritize.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to select a preferred industry expert or publication based on your personal trust and reading preferences.

questions.question: What topic do you want to search for?
questions.why: The search bar prompts for topics, locations, or sources, requiring you to specify the exact subject you want to read about.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to choose a news topic that aligns with your personal interests or immediate curiosity.

questions.question: Does the results page heading show the searched topic?
questions.why: Confirming that the timeline updates to 'Health News' ensures the platform correctly processed your specific query.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means losing the ability to personally verify that the search results accurately reflect the exact topic you had in mind.

children.label: Narrow the results
children.note: 3.4.1 first on a general engine. 3.4.2 to 3.4.4 in any order, each applied, inspected, and reverted before the next (vLA0) - only 3.4.5 sticks. 3.4.3 is also how the newsroom keeper reaches text advisories (AE9a).

questions.question: Are the current results old or from non-news sites?
questions.why: The screen showed outdated articles from May 2018 and non-news links like Wikipedia, meaning the default search results did not meet the requirement for recent news.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the control to decide whether to refine the search using built-in platform tools or by manually modifying the search keywords.

questions.question: Are you still on the 'News' tab for your search results?
questions.why: The screen shows the 'All' tab underlined in blue and a Wikipedia article as the top result, indicating general web results instead of news.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the assurance that the agent is actually looking at news articles rather than general web results.

questions.question: Which sort order is selected, date or relevance?
questions.why: The dropdown menu offers both 'Sorted by date' and 'Sorted by relevance', forcing a choice between seeing the absolute newest articles or the most topically accurate ones first.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide whether strict recency or topical relevance is more important for your specific news search.

questions.question: Did your filter restrict the search results to only show blog posts?
questions.why: The first result displayed was a 2018 blog post, indicating that the current search parameters might be excluding authoritative recent news.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to notice that a filter is returning outdated blog content instead of actual news and decide to revert it.

questions.question: Which media-type checkboxes are selected in the filter?
questions.why: The screen displays checkboxes for 'Video' and 'Advisories', allowing you to remove unwanted media formats from the search results.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to specify your preferred media format for consuming the news.

questions.question: Which time window is selected in the date filter?
questions.why: The dropdown offers multiple time frames like 'Past hour' or 'Past month', which determines how recent the news articles must be to appear in your results.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means the agent might pick a time frame that is too broad or too narrow for your specific information needs.

questions.question: Did the filter return older articles?
questions.why: Seeing older dates like 2017 and 2013 on the search results confirms that the archive filter is functioning correctly.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the visual confirmation that the platform's date filters are actually working as intended before selecting an article.

questions.question: Does the date filter match the years you entered?
questions.why: Verifying that the system expanded your input of '1990' and '1999' to the full calendar years ensures your search covers the entire intended timeframe.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to verify that the system's automatic date formatting perfectly aligns with their intended search boundaries.

questions.question: Do the article timestamps actually match the 'Today' filter?
questions.why: The interface suggests the content is from today, but the visible timestamps reveal articles ranging from 17 hours to 5 days old.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the assurance of getting truly recent news if the agent blindly trusts the category label instead of verifying the actual publication dates.

children.label: Compare the outlets on a story

questions.question: Does the story card offer a Full Coverage view with more outlets?
questions.why: The news card features a 'Full Coverage' button alongside related links from different publishers, offering a way to expand on the main headline.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the chance to spontaneously decide how deeply they want to explore a specific news event based on the available sources.

children.label: Check the advisories for coming footage

questions.question: What delivery time and content does the advisory pane list for the upcoming footage?
questions.why: The details pane on the right reveals the specific description and expected delivery time for the upcoming news.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to know exactly when the upcoming news footage will become available.

children.label: Read the story
children.note: 4.1 from any list; 4.2, then 4.3 when the preview runs out - four reads finish on the source site, two stay in the preview. 4.4 for video items. 4.5 closes the loop every time, by whichever door the surface gives.

questions.question: Which of these recent business articles do you want to open?
questions.why: The screen displays the 'Latest' business tab with articles from 5 to 6 hours ago, providing the necessary options to select and open a current story.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the chance to personally pick the specific business headline that most appeals to their current interests.

questions.question: Does the content of the opened article match the preview snippet from the search results?
questions.why: Verifying that the article text matches the preview snippet ensures you have opened the correct article.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user receives incorrect information if the agent opens an article that doesn't match the expected content from the search results.

questions.question: Is the full article text visible, or cut off with a link to the source site?
questions.why: The screen showed the title and subtitle, but the author's name and the rest of the text were cut off.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user misses the actual news content if the agent stops before the article fully loads.

questions.question: Are you currently viewing the opened article or still browsing the aggregator's feed?
questions.why: The screen shows the active tab is the Guardian article, contradicting the claim that the aggregator feed is being scrolled.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses accurate tracking of whether the agent has successfully opened the target article or is still searching the feed.

questions.question: Does the video playing in the pop-up match the news article you intended to open?
questions.why: Clicking the video thumbnail opens a pop-up player, making it necessary to confirm the video actually covers the specific news topic you selected.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the immediate visual confirmation that the pop-up video is the correct news story rather than an unrelated clip or ad.

children.label: Save and curate the stories
children.note: 5.1 before the first save. 5.2 or 5.3 - 5.4 inside 5.3 on a first board. 5.5 after a save: the same check succeeds in one keeper and comes back empty in another. 5.6 then 5.7 only in the keeper that unwinds its own work (xbgg).

children.label: Review the save and share options

questions.question: Which save and share actions does the toolbar offer?
questions.why: The action bar displays numerous options like saving to a board, emailing, or sharing to social media, offering ways to retain or distribute the information.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to organically decide to save or share an interesting article to your personal networks or reading lists.

questions.question: Does the page show a read-later save control next to the article?
questions.why: The screen displayed a "Read Later" bookmark icon next to the article, offering the option to save it.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to curate a reading list of interesting articles for future reference.

children.label: Save the story to a board

questions.question: Which board does the save dialog show the article going to?
questions.why: The star icon opens a modal to organize saved articles by project or topic, letting you create a custom board to easily find the article again.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally name the board and define the organizational structure for your saved news.

questions.question: Does the page ask for a name for the new board?
questions.why: The screen displays a 'Board name' popup that requires a custom text entry to organize the saved article.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means the agent might choose a generic board name that does not fit your personal organizational system.

questions.question: Is the article you saved earlier visible in the Read Later section?
questions.why: The screen displays 'No Read Later Stories Yet', indicating that the article you attempted to save earlier was not successfully added to the list.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose access to the specific article you intended to read because the agent moves on to a different section instead of verifying why the save action failed.

children.label: Remove the story from the board

questions.question: Are you sure you want to delete the entire board?
questions.why: The '...' dropdown menu displays both harmless sorting options like 'Latest' and the destructive 'Delete' option, requiring careful selection.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to prevent the permanent deletion of their curated board if the agent mistakenly chooses the wrong menu item.

children.label: Download and import the footage
children.note: 6.1, then 6.2 and 6.3 in the browser, 6.4 to 6.6 in the editor, 6.7 when playback stutters. one keeper runs it (AE9a), and the task ends with the transcode still at 12 percent.

questions.question: Which specific search result should you select from the list?
questions.why: The results show multiple recent items with different media types and topics, such as a video about Russian ice hockey versus one about India's IOC ban, requiring a choice based on relevance.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally select the specific sub-topic and media format that best fits your current interest.

questions.question: Does this video and its accompanying transcript contain the specific footage and story details you need?
questions.why: Checking the video player and the text sections like 'SHOWS:' and 'STORY:' confirms whether the asset actually contains the relevant footage and information about the Russian hockey team.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally watch the video and read the transcript to ensure the footage and story nuances meet your exact expectations.

questions.question: Which files does the download menu have selected by default?
questions.why: The download menu defaults to including XML and other metadata, but selecting only the video file saves storage and bandwidth if you are writing your own story.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to prevent the agent from downloading unnecessary metadata files that clutter your local storage.

children.label: Name the file and keep the extension

questions.question: What filename and extension does the save dialog show?
questions.why: The default filename is a cryptic string of characters, so renaming it and keeping the extension visible makes the file much easier to identify later.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to apply their own personal naming conventions and organizational preferences to downloaded files.

questions.question: Does the import dialog have the copy-to-library option selected?
questions.why: The import settings dialog requires deciding whether to copy files to the local events folder to prevent losing access if the original drive is disconnected.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses control over their local file management and the assurance that media is safely stored on their primary hard drive.

children.label: Place the clip on the timeline

questions.question: What progress does the Background Tasks window show for the import?
questions.why: The Background Tasks window shows the media import is at 12%, which helps determine how much longer the process will take.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to monitor the exact progress of the background import and decide whether to wait for it to finish.

questions.question: Does the Background Tasks window show the media still transcoding?
questions.why: The screen showed choppy playback of a high-resolution file, which prompted an investigation into background tasks.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: A person delegating to an agent loses the ability to visually assess playback quality and intuitively troubleshoot system performance issues.

children.label: Close the session
children.note: 7.1 then 7.2. one keeper does both (v4vm); the rest stop the recorder or just stop.

questions.question: Did you log out of the account?
questions.why: The screen displays a promotional landing page with a 'LOGIN' button, confirming that the active session has ended.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the assurance that their personal account was securely closed and their session data protected at the end of the task.

patientportal.task: use a patient portal (MyChart, FollowMyHealth, LabCorp or Quest portals, a health system's own portal): sign in and complete one concrete arc — view test results, read or send a message to the care team, view or download a visit summary or medical record, or check in for an upcoming visit; complete when the result, message, or record is on screen. Surface pinned: the portal itself — not symptom research (healthinfo), not appointment booking (doctor), not pharmacy refills (refill).

tree.label: Use the patient portal
tree.note: do 1 - 1.2 once, on a first invitation (L1Mf); 1.3 thereafter. then 2, and from 2 whichever of 3 to 6 the day's task is - each keeper walks one to three, none walks all four. 7 after any commit: 3.13, 5.9, 5.10.4, and 6.5 all hand into it. 4 gates on 3 at some clinics (CkVD: eCheck-In must complete before joining) and not others (fW6G: abandoned with Finish later, and the visit proceeds). 8 as needed and at the end.

children.label: Get into the portal
children.note: 1.1 where the portal is reached through the clinic's site or an email (FE1_, L1Mf). 1.2 replaces 1.3 on the invited first run and hands straight into the session. otherwise 1.3, with 1.4 as the browser interjects. FE1_ runs 1.3 twice by design - it signs out mid-demo and back in.

questions.question: Should you allow the app to send you notifications?
questions.why: The system prompts you to allow or deny notifications, which include alerts and badges that can notify you of upcoming appointments.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to control whether this medical app is allowed to interrupt you with push notifications on your personal device.

questions.question: Should you allow the app to access your calendar for appointment reminders?
questions.why: The system prompt asks for permission to access your calendar in order to schedule appointment reminders.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to decide whether their medical appointments are automatically synced to their personal device calendar.

questions.question: Which portal tab should you select to view a different history of lab results?
questions.why: The browser displays multiple tabs for different patient portals, so you must identify which one contains the specific lab history you need.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The agent might click into the wrong portal and retrieve an incomplete or incorrect set of lab results.

questions.question: What is the exact web address you use to access the portal?
questions.why: The screen showed the address bar with 'mycarecorner.net', highlighting the importance of using the '.net' extension instead of a traditional '.com'.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the specific knowledge of the correct domain extension needed to access their patient portal securely.

children.label: Register from the invitation
children.note: 1.2.1 to 1.2.4 in order - the code and the verification answer both come from the same email-and-form loop. then 1.2.5 and 1.2.6: two separate consent gates after the account already exists.

questions.question: Is the activation link about to be opened genuinely from your provider, and still inside the window the email states?
questions.why: The email contains a specific, time-sensitive link that must be clicked within 24 hours to access the portal and create your account.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to verify the sender's address and ensure the activation link is a legitimate portal URL rather than a phishing attempt.

questions.question: Are you ready to continue the information transfer to MyCareCorner?
questions.why: The screen prompts you to continue the transfer process, which involves signing in or creating a Connected Health Base account to store your records.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to decide whether you actually want your sensitive medical records transferred to and stored on this specific third-party platform.

questions.question: Is the required identity code correctly entered so you can submit it?
questions.why: The screen shows an auto-filled identity code required to transfer your health information to MyCareCorner, which needs to be verified before submission.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the assurance of personally verifying that the correct security code from your private communications was used to access your sensitive health data.

questions.question: Are you ready to submit the registration form and create your account?
questions.why: The screen displays a 'Create Account' button, indicating that the registration details are ready to be submitted.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to review their personal information for accuracy before the account is finalized.

questions.question: What personal information will you provide to create your account?
questions.why: The registration form requires sensitive details like your date of birth, sex, and email address to establish your health portal identity.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose control over exactly which optional fields, like the profile image, are skipped or filled with your personal data.

questions.question: What is the answer to your security question?
questions.why: The screen requires the correct answer to a pre-selected security question to verify your identity before granting access to the account.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent would not know the private answer to your personal security question, preventing it from successfully signing in.

questions.question: Which patient record is selected, and what access level does the page request?
questions.why: The screen requires selecting a specific patient record and granting the hospital permission to view and change your health information.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to review the requested permissions and make an informed decision about sharing their health data.

questions.question: Do you agree to the terms of use to continue?
questions.why: The screen requires you to accept a long Terms of Use Agreement before you can proceed into the patient portal.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose the chance to review how the portal handles your sensitive health data before legally agreeing to their terms.

questions.question: Do you consent to the U.S. Government system use policy?
questions.why: The screen presents a mandatory U.S. Government system use policy warning that your activity is subject to monitoring and lacks privacy expectations.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to read and personally consent to the government's strict monitoring and data privacy terms before accessing their health records.

questions.question: Do you want to sign in using the pre-filled credentials?
questions.why: The email and password fields are already populated with saved credentials, so you must decide whether to accept them or enter different information.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to verify exactly which account is being accessed before the agent submits the saved login details.

questions.question: Has your session timed out?
questions.why: The Labcorp OnDemand login page displays a banner stating you have been logged out due to inactivity.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the awareness that their session expired and they must re-authenticate to access their health information.

questions.question: Should you allow the browser to save your login credentials for this site?
questions.why: The screen showed a Google Chrome prompt asking whether to save the password for the patient portal.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: A person delegating to an agent loses the ability to decide whether their sensitive health portal credentials are saved in the browser.

children.label: Find the task
children.note: 2.1, then 2.2 past whatever the feed stacks on top, then 2.3 for visit tasks - the other destinations open from the nav or a widget, and their entry ops sit in their own goals. re-entered between tasks: FE1_ returns here after each subtask, g18A comes back through Home to reach the inbox.

questions.question: Are there new results on the dashboard, or do you need to click to view all past records?
questions.why: The dashboard states there are no new results to view, meaning you must navigate to the full history to find older reports.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the immediate reassurance of seeing that they have no new or unread test results pending.

questions.question: Are you viewing the records for the correct patient?
questions.why: The dashboard explicitly shows 'dbase2 Test' and a birth date of 'October 2, 1977', confirming whose medical information is currently active.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to personally verify that the agent is accessing the correct individual's sensitive health records.

questions.question: Which appointment are you selecting to start your televisit?
questions.why: The screen lists your upcoming appointments, requiring you to identify the correct provider, date, and time to ensure you join the right session.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you miss the chance to personally verify the provider and schedule details before entering the virtual waiting room.

questions.question: Are the listed upcoming appointments active?
questions.why: The 'UPCOMING APPOINTMENTS' section lists two appointments, but both are marked as canceled.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the awareness that their appointments have been canceled and cannot be checked into.

children.label: Check in for the visit
children.note: 3.1 opens it. then the verify stages in the order the clinic fixes, each closed by its own this-information-is-correct gate: iEZR runs 3.2, 3.5, 3.6, 3.7 to 3.9, 3.11, then 3.12; jNEa runs 3.3, 3.4, 3.6 to 3.11, then 3.12 three times over; CkVD shows only 3.6 before the video cuts. 3.13 ends it - or Finish later abandons it at any stage (fW6G, at 3.2).

questions.question: How much of your outstanding balance and copay do you want to pay today?
questions.why: The check-in screen presents options to pay just the $5.00 copay, the full $195.00 balance, or to pay later.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means losing control over your immediate cash flow and how your medical debts are prioritized.

questions.question: Is the option to save your payment method for future visits pre-checked?
questions.why: The screen presents a $5.00 amount due with options to use Apple Pay or a card, along with a pre-checked box to save the payment method for future use.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means the agent might use an undesired payment method or leave the default setting checked, saving your financial details to the portal without explicit consent.

questions.question: Does the check-in text name the expected patient and clinic?
questions.why: The text message specifies it is for Shannon's appointment at Rainbow Pediatric Center, so you must verify this matches the intended patient and visit before clicking the link to begin check-in.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the opportunity to personally verify that the check-in link corresponds to the correct patient and appointment details before proceeding.

questions.question: Which button do you select to start your check-in?
questions.why: The screen offers both 'BEGIN CHECK-IN' for pre-visit tasks and 'I have arrived' for the day of the appointment, requiring you to choose the correct option based on the current date.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means an agent might incorrectly notify the clinic of your arrival before the actual appointment day.

questions.question: Is your pre-filled contact information correct?
questions.why: The portal displays your current address, phone numbers, and email, giving you the chance to verify or edit them before proceeding.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the opportunity to catch and correct outdated contact details in your medical record.

questions.question: Do you want to add a new emergency contact, or does the current list look good?
questions.why: The portal asks you to review your emergency and PHI disclosure contacts, offering options to add a new one or confirm the existing list.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to designate a new trusted individual to receive emergency updates or discuss their medical information.

questions.question: Which consent forms do you need to review and sign?
questions.why: The screen requires a signature on the MyChart Virtual Visit Consent form before allowing you to continue to the visit.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose the opportunity to personally read and understand the legal and medical terms of the consent form being signed on your behalf.

questions.question: How will you provide the required images of your insurance card?
questions.why: The screen prompts you to capture front and back images of your insurance card to verify your coverage for the visit.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent cannot physically use your device's camera to take pictures of your actual insurance card.

questions.question: Do you need to add a new insurance policy?
questions.why: The screen displays the current insurance on file and provides options to add a new policy or pay out of pocket.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The agent cannot physically photograph your new insurance card or know if your coverage has changed.

questions.question: Which of these listed medications are you currently taking?
questions.why: The medication reconciliation screen requires you to confirm whether you are taking, not taking, or changing the dosage for each prescribed drug.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means losing the opportunity to accurately communicate your current medication habits to your care team, which could lead to unsafe prescribing decisions.

questions.question: Is the allergy information accurate?
questions.why: The screen requires you to confirm that having no allergies on file is correct before proceeding with the check-in.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might automatically confirm the lack of allergies without knowing your actual medical history, potentially risking your safety during future treatments.

children.label: Answer the questionnaires
children.note: whichever the clinic attaches: 3.12.1 to 3.12.3 as one three-step history (iEZR); 3.12.4 to 3.12.6 as separate loops (jNEa). each closes with 3.12.7 before its own submit.

questions.question: What does this check-in questionnaire ask, and what are your answers?
questions.why: The screen presents a comprehensive list of body systems to check for any current symptoms before the televisit.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent accepting the default 'No' for all symptoms could fail to report important health issues you are currently experiencing.

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the chance to explicitly confirm their medical history, risking inaccurate default data being submitted to their provider.

questions.question: Are you ready to submit your medical forms and finish checking in?
questions.why: The screen shows the interim history form and a list of completed medical questionnaires required to finalize your visit check-in.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose the opportunity to personally verify the accuracy of your health history before it is submitted to the clinic.

children.label: Join the video visit

CkVD's join button goes green only after 3 completes and the clock reaches ten minutes before the start.

questions.question: Which practices are you enrolling with for tele-visits, and is the information correct?
questions.why: The screen lists practices eligible for h2h audio and video calls and requires confirming enrollment.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to verify which specific medical practices they are authorizing for telehealth communications.

questions.question: Do you want to confirm ending the TeleVisit?
questions.why: The screen displays a confirmation popup asking if you are sure you want to end the TeleVisit, which will permanently close the active video session.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the ability to personally ensure all your medical questions were answered by the provider before disconnecting the call.

questions.question: When do you want to be reminded about this appointment?
questions.why: The screen offers several reminder intervals ranging from one hour to one week in advance, as well as an option to opt out entirely.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means the agent might set a reminder that interrupts you unnecessarily or fails to remind you when you actually need it.

questions.question: Are you going to be able to make it to this appointment?
questions.why: The portal requires you to confirm your attendance or choose to reschedule or cancel the upcoming visit.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to evaluate their schedule and decide whether to keep or change the appointment.

questions.question: Should I test my camera and microphone?
questions.why: The screen recommends testing your device's camera and microphone to ensure a good connection before the video call.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to verify that their physical hardware is functioning properly for their telehealth appointment.

questions.question: Does the page show a live picture from the camera?
questions.why: The screen requires you to visually confirm that your camera is working properly before proceeding.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent cannot see your physical screen to verify that the camera is successfully capturing your video.

questions.question: Are you ready to start the televisit?
questions.why: The screen shows a button to start the televisit, which will launch the video interface and potentially connect you directly to your provider.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means the agent might launch the live video feed before you are physically present and ready to speak with your doctor.

questions.question: Is the system ready for you to join the video visit?
questions.why: The 'BEGIN VIDEO VISIT' button remains greyed out until 15 minutes before the appointment, so you must wait for it to turn green to proceed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you miss the immediate visual confirmation that your appointment is starting and the direct transition into the virtual consultation room.

questions.question: Which visit's waiting room does the page say you are in?
questions.why: The screen confirms you are waiting for the other participant to join the Community Health Network video visit and provides controls to mute or hide your video.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the ability to personally verify your camera and microphone readiness before the doctor appears on screen.

questions.question: Should you wait for the provider to reconnect or exit the TeleVisit?
questions.why: A popup indicates that the provider disconnected unexpectedly and asks if you want to wait for them to rejoin or exit the visit.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to decide how long they are willing to wait for a disconnected provider before abandoning the telehealth appointment.

children.label: Message the care team
children.note: 5.1 when the inbox holds something. to send: 5.2, then 5.3 to 5.6 down the form, 5.7 and 5.8, then 5.9. 5.10 where the platform gives appointment requests their own form (FE1_) - on MyCareCorner the same composer carries them as message types instead. the reply is asynchronous; checking it is 7.3.

questions.question: How do you prefer to be contacted if follow-up is needed?
questions.why: The form requires choosing between a secure message or a phone call for any necessary follow-up communication.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to dictate their preferred communication channel, risking missed updates or inconvenient phone calls.

questions.question: Which message do you want to open?
questions.why: The inbox displays a new message from Betty Larson regarding a referral appointment, requiring you to select which communication to review.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the ability to prioritize which provider communications to read first based on your current health concerns.

questions.question: Do you need to reply to this message from your care team?
questions.why: The message asks if you have scheduled your cardiology referral appointment, requiring you to decide whether to respond or simply close the panel.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means an agent decides whether to update your care team about the status of your personal medical appointments.

questions.question: Which patient are you sending this message on behalf of?
questions.why: The screen features a required patient dropdown, meaning you must specify exactly whose medical record this message is about.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the oversight to guarantee the message is sent on behalf of the correct family member or dependent.

questions.question: Which doctor do you want to send this message to?
questions.why: The portal requires selecting a specific recipient from a long dropdown list of medical staff to ensure the message reaches the correct care team member.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means the agent might select the wrong provider from the list, potentially delaying care or sending sensitive medical information to the wrong staff member.

questions.question: Which type of message are you sending?
questions.why: The dropdown requires selecting between a chart correction and a clinical message to properly route your inquiry.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Letting an agent choose the message type means they might miscategorize your inquiry, leading to delays in reaching the correct care team member.

questions.question: What exactly do you want to say in your message to the care team?
questions.why: The empty message field requires you to clearly articulate your specific health question or concern so the provider can give accurate advice.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means losing the ability to personally describe your specific symptoms, nuances, and concerns directly to your doctor.

questions.question: Do you need to attach any files before sending the message?
questions.why: The message form includes an option to attach files from your computer or MyCareCorner before clicking send.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the opportunity to decide if a specific personal document or photo should be included to support your request.

questions.question: Do you agree to the terms required to send this message?
questions.why: The screen requires you to acknowledge that the message is not for emergencies and may take up to two business days for a response before it can be sent.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this to an agent means you lose the opportunity to personally review and accept the specific response timeframes and emergency disclaimers for your medical communication.

questions.question: Is your message complete and ready to send to your provider?
questions.why: The screen shows 'Cancel' and 'SEND' buttons, marking the final opportunity to review the message before it goes to the care team.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means losing the chance to personally verify the tone and accuracy of the medical information being sent to your doctor.

children.label: Request an appointment

questions.question: What details should I provide in the appointment request form?
questions.why: The screen displays multiple fields that need to be filled, including the provider, preferred dates and times, and the reason for the visit.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to specify your exact scheduling preferences and the private medical reason for your visit.

questions.question: Did the 'Appointment Message Sent' confirmation actually appear after the request was submitted?
questions.why: Clicking the button officially submits your request to the care team, which is confirmed when the 'Appointment Message Sent' text appears on screen.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the immediate reassurance of seeing the confirmation text that proves your appointment request was successfully sent.

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide whether to focus on recent changes or review your entire long-term health trend for this specific test.

questions.question: Is the full document list open, or only the recent files the dashboard shows by default?
questions.why: The dashboard displayed a limited list of recent files, so clicking 'View All Files' ensures you can find older or specific documents not immediately visible.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to see which specific files the portal highlights on the dashboard before opening the full document repository.

questions.question: Are there any COVID-19 records currently available on your account?

questions.question: Do you want to filter the displayed allergies by a specific date range?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to specify exactly which time period of medical data they want to review.

questions.question: Which of the listed records do you want to open?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might select an older report instead of the most recent one, causing you to review outdated health information.

questions.question: Do you want to view the detailed results for this specific test?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to privately review your metabolic panel results firsthand before a third party accesses your sensitive health data.

questions.question: What details should you provide for the new allergy?
questions.why: The form requires specific details like the allergen type and reaction, but warns that this data will not be seen by your healthcare team.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might guess or omit details about your specific allergic reactions and dates, leading to an inaccurate personal health record.

questions.question: Did you apply the correct condition, provider, and personal tags before saving the record?
questions.why: The screen displays fields for the condition, provider, and custom tags like '#April2017', which dictate how this lab report will be organized and retrieved later.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means losing the ability to use your own personalized tagging system to organize your private health records.

questions.question: Should you download a PDF copy of these results for your personal records?

stock.task: buy a specific amount of a stock or crypto in a retail app (Robinhood, Coinbase, Fidelity, Cash App): search the ticker, enter a dollar amount or share count, review the order (price, fees), place it, and see the filled or pending confirmation; complete when the order confirmation is on screen. Surface pinned: a retail brokerage or crypto app or website. Variants: trading-strategy and technical-analysis content, price-prediction videos, and day-trading courses do not belong.

tree.label: Trade on an investing app
tree.note: do 1. 2 fires wherever the platform puts the wall: before the first buy (yeKU), inside the first buy (Wopd), only at send (DZKH), once per ramp even twice in one session (lBbZ). 3.1 every session; the rest of 3 as the rails demand. repeat 4 until an asset settles - 4.8 ends an orbit without a trade. then 5 and 6 as a pair, once per trade: four keepers run the pair twice, buy then sell (DZKH, eVJg, ZWfJ, lBbZ), and ten keepers run 5 without ever reaching 5.11. 7 when the holdings leave the platform (O1Ka, fDjD, lBbZ). 8 and 9 stand apart from any single trade and take over whole stretches of a session (w-mD, jH1r).

children.label: Get into the platform
children.note: 1.1 then 1.7 - most keepers arrive signed in and 1.2 to 1.6 never fire. 1.2 to 1.5 on a first run (yeKU walks all of it; frXh chooses among managed tiers first). 1.6 recurs when a session lapses mid-task (yeKU signs back in after the 3-day wait). 1.8 swaps the whole session onto simulated money (JAFQ).

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means you lose the ability to decide whether your funds are placed in a self-directed account or a robo-advisor managed account like Fidelity Go.

questions.question: What personal details must you enter to begin the account sign-up process?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to privately set your own password and control the initial disclosure of your personal contact information.

questions.question: Is your account set up and ready for your first purchase?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the reassurance of personally confirming that your new financial account was set up correctly and securely before funding it.

questions.question: Do you see the verification email from Coinbase?
questions.why: The screen shows an unread email from Coinbase, which must be opened to verify your account before you can proceed with trading.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step requires giving an agent access to your personal email inbox, which exposes your private communications and other accounts.

questions.question: Do you agree to the user agreement and its stated financial risks?
questions.why: The screen presents a binding contract outlining significant financial risks, such as transaction reversals and dispute policies, which must be accepted to proceed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the chance to read and evaluate the specific legal and financial risks they are legally binding themselves to.

questions.question: Which credentials should you use to sign into your account?
questions.why: The screen displays a sign-in form requiring an email and password to access the account and continue the process.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means handing over your private email and password to a third party.

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the peace of mind of confirming the agent is using the paper trading environment rather than risking your real funds.

questions.question: Are you comfortable leaving your two-factor authentication set to the currently enabled authenticator app?

Variants: solving the issue through FAQ self-service, and the substantive dispute after the agent is reached, do not belong.

tracking.task: track a package or order (Amazon orders, UPS/FedEx/USPS tracking): find the tracking entry from the order — or enter the tracking number on the carrier site — open the status page, read the scan history, and interpret where the package is and when it will arrive; complete when the current status and expected delivery are on screen and read out. Surface pinned: a carrier tracking page or retailer order-status page on web or app. Variants: filing claims for lost packages, and receiving or verifying the delivery at the door, do not belong.

tree.note: 1 on every run - most runs start in a search box or an app icon. then 2 on a retailer or tracker-app surface, where the shipment is already listed, or 3 then 4 on a carrier surface, where the user has to bring the number - GHCW runs both, in that order, and gets less from the second. 5 whenever a status page loads; five keepers never get there and stop at the form in 4. 6 alongside 5 wherever a second source is on screen. 7 after the read where the surface offers it; pKsL spends most of its time there.

tutoring.task: find and book a tutor on a tutoring platform (Preply, Wyzant, italki, Varsity Tutors, Cambly, Outschool): search by subject or language, compare tutors on rates, reviews, and intro videos, pick one, and book or schedule a trial or lesson through to the booking confirmation; complete when the booked-lesson confirmation is on screen. Surface pinned: the CLIENT-side booking flow — tutor-side content (how to become a tutor, earnings) is off-task.

tree.label: Find and book a tutor
tree.note: 1 where the platform demands an account - at the door (jHfA, i3ok, XyTV, KIjj, cDu8, 7RrY), or only when the booking button is pressed (CWIs, cDu8's email gate, 7jo_'s verify wall); half the keepers arrive signed in. 2 before any lesson on the credit platforms (jHfA, i3ok), when the wall fires inside 7 (jMRd), or after a trial to prepay hours (zym-). then 3, then 4 as far as the user bothers - filters are opened far more often than applied. 5 picks one tutor and 5.5 reads it; a profile that fails loops back to 5.1. 6 configures the lesson, with 6.6 for the time. 7 commits in one of three ways set by the platform: pay from the wallet and wait for the tutor (italki), pay at a checkout (Preply, the plan credit in 7RrY), or send a message request and pay later (Wyzant). 8 reads whatever follows, which on italki and Wyzant is a pending request. two keepers skip 3 to 5 and start on a chosen tutor (htcf, jHfA's recommended shortcut).

children.note: 1.1, then 1.2 or 1.3; 1.4 to 1.6 on a new account as the platform asks. 1.7 when the gate fires later, at the booking button - it can interrupt 7. 1.8 on the one keeper who lands on the wrong account type. 1.9 where offered, before the search, on the one keeper who opens settings.

questions.question: Do you already have an account here, or should I set up a new one?

questions.question: Does the sign-up page carry the free first hour promotion shown on the homepage?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the financial benefit of a promotional discount if the agent defaults to the standard signup flow instead of hunting for the special offer.

questions.question: Does the page promise a credit bonus for arriving through this link?

usedcar.task: research and price a used car as a buyer: set the search filters that matter (make/model, year range, budget, mileage, drivetrain), browse the matching listings, open a specific listing and check its history and price rating, and get a price estimate or value for a specific vehicle; complete when a specific car's listing with its price evaluation (e.g. good/fair deal rating or KBB value) is on screen. Surface pinned: a used-car marketplace or pricing site (KBB, CarGurus, Carvana, AutoTrader, Edmunds). Variants: car-dealer/dealership-side content, car-flipping or reselling business content, car review vlogs with driving footage, and mechanic-inspection videos do not belong.

tree.label: Research and price a used car
tree.note: 1 on every site and tool the session opens - most open several. 2 then 3 on a marketplace, with 3.5 sending the search back into 2.10 when the list is too long, too short or wrongly ordered. 4 on an opened listing, 4.9 where a history link exists. 5 where a value is wanted - fed from 4.8 when the car is a listing, from memory when it is the user's own car. 6 is the loop most keepers run: it re-runs 2 to 4 on the next site or 5 on the next tool and carries the numbers between them. 7 after any 4 or 5, and again after 6. 8 in three keepers only. The task as asked ends at 7.

children.label: Reach the car site
children.note: 1.1 then 1.2 on every site; 1.3 whenever a prompt appears, which is at any point in the task; 1.4 when the site has a country edition. 1.5 is never done on camera.

questions.question: Which of the car sites listed on the results page will the search use?
questions.why: This matters because the screen lists four specific URLs, highlighting that different platforms offer distinct advantages like better pricing deals or free vehicle history reports.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to choose their preferred platform based on their personal priority between finding the best price deals or securing free vehicle history reports.

questions.question: Is the site that opened the official appraisal site, and not a sponsored ad or lookalike from the search results?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to verify that the agent selected the authentic appraisal website instead of a misleading ad.

questions.question: Which entry paths does the homepage offer, and which one leads to listings?
questions.why: The homepage presents distinct paths to either find a used car or get a CARFAX report, determining how your new search begins.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to decide whether to browse new listings or pull a report for a specific car you already have in mind.
