questions.why: The dropdown defaults to new cars, so you must explicitly select the used option to ensure you are pricing the correct type of vehicle.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the opportunity to consider certified pre-owned alternatives instead of standard used cars.

questions.question: Is there a warning about opening many tabs at once?
questions.why: The modal warns that proceeding will open 31 separate tabs for Craigslist results and requires pop-ups to be allowed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to decide if opening 31 separate tabs will overwhelm your browser or if you prefer to keep the warning active.

questions.question: Is an ad banner covering part of the results?
questions.why: Reviewing the 13 results for the BMW M8 Gran Coupe ensures they match your search, while closing the ad banner at the bottom reveals more of the page.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to notice that the first result is actually a new car rather than a used one and to manually dismiss the ad banner blocking the listings.

questions.question: Is this the right country's edition of the site for where you are?
questions.why: The screen showed the US version of Kelley Blue Book, which would not provide accurate pricing for a Canadian buyer.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the assurance that the pricing data applies to their local market.

questions.question: Does this page offer a price tool for regular buyers, or only for dealers?
questions.why: The kbb.ca homepage displayed a message indicating it currently only offers B2B solutions and lacks a consumer-facing tool.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to realize the site is non-functional for consumers and pivot to a working alternative.

questions.why: The screen displays a Google sign-in popup, requiring a choice between linking your personal account or dismissing it to browse anonymously.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to decide whether to protect your privacy or share your personal Google account details with the platform.

Several keepers arrive with all of this already applied (e3a9 on four sites) and only 2.7 shows on camera.

questions.question: Do the points on the graph open real listings?

questions.question: Does the price on the opened listing match the price shown in the preview?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: If the agent fails to verify price consistency across pages, you might base your purchasing decision on inaccurate or misleading pricing information.

questions.question: Is the advertised mileage realistic for the vehicle's age, or could it be a typo?
questions.why: The listing claims a 1999 vehicle has only 2,500 miles, which is highly suspicious and likely a typo by the seller (e.g., missing a zero) that drastically skews the car's perceived value.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The agent might overvalue the car based on an impossibly low mileage figure, failing to apply the common sense needed to spot a seller's typo.

questions.question: Does the savings figure equal the value minus the asking price?
questions.why: Confirming the math between the estimated value and the dealer price ensures the advertised savings are accurate and not misleading.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally verify the math behind the advertised deal to ensure the platform isn't misrepresenting the actual savings.

questions.question: Does the price gauge put this price below, within, or above the fair range?
questions.why: Pricing tools often use a visual gauge or slider to show exactly where a specific price falls within a broader market range, providing context that a single raw number lacks.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the intuitive visual context of whether the asking price is at the very top, middle, or bottom of the acceptable market range.

questions.question: Should you swipe through the full image galleries for these listings?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to visually inspect the vehicle's interior and exterior condition before deciding which listing to pursue.

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent relying solely on the text metadata might select a car that lacks the specific premium features you requested.

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user ends up pursuing a car that is actually thousands of dollars over their budget once the hidden stipulations are applied.

questions.why: Private sellers sometimes engage in 'title jumping' by selling a car they never legally registered, which can trap the buyer in a DMV nightmare when trying to transfer ownership.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user risks handing over cash for a vehicle they cannot legally register or insure because the agent failed to verify the legal legitimacy of the seller's title status.

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means you lose the ability to prioritize between a quick dealership quote and a potentially higher private-party valuation based on your personal goals.

questions.question: Is the price estimate set for a dealer sale or a private sale, and which is this car?
questions.why: The screen provides different fair market ranges and purchase prices depending on whether you buy from a dealer, a certified dealer, or a private party.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to compare the estimated costs of buying from a private seller versus a dealership.

questions.question: Which body-style category fits this car on the pricing page?
questions.why: The screen presents overlapping categories like 'Coupe' and 'Sports Car', requiring a decision on how the site classifies this specific vehicle.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to decide whether to prioritize the vehicle's structural shape or its performance class when navigating the site's categorization system.

questions.question: Do the year, make and model in the form match the listing?
questions.why: The screen showed the completed form with 'Used', '2012', 'Audi', and 'A6' selected, indicating the criteria were ready to submit.

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to ensure the price estimate accurately reflects the exact engine and trim level of the vehicle you are researching.

questions.question: Does the colour picked in the pricing tool match the listing?
questions.why: Applying the specific silver color from the listing to the TrueCar calculator dropped the base estimate by $325, showing that exact features directly change the true market value.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the transparency of seeing exactly how individual features like paint color positively or negatively adjust the vehicle's final valuation.

questions.question: Do the options ticked on the pricing form match what the listing shows?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to verify that all specific vehicle features and conditions were accurately selected before generating the final valuation.

questions.question: Does the mileage entered match the listing's mileage?

questions.question: Does the ZIP on the pricing page match where the car is, or where you are?
questions.why: The pricing table calculates a specific regional adjustment and total market value based on the currently entered zip code.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the guarantee that the final price estimate accurately reflects the specific local market where you plan to buy the car.

questions.question: Do the accident and damage answers match what the history report says?
questions.why: The TrueCar page requires specific declarations about accidents, damage, mechanical issues, and warning lights to generate an accurate evaluation.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the reliability of the final price estimate if the agent blindly selects 'No' for condition issues without verifying them in the listing.

questions.question: Does the form ask whether you're the first owner and still paying it off?
questions.why: The screen asks if you are the original owner, still making payments, and looking to buy a replacement to complete the vehicle details form.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: If the agent guesses these details, it might calculate an inaccurate value based on incorrect equity assumptions or trigger unwanted sales leads.

questions.question: What does the form ask for before it moves on?
questions.why: The screen prompts for the make, model, year, and buying timeframe to progress the vehicle inquiry form.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose control over the specific vehicle details and purchasing timeline communicated to the dealership.

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to decide whether to share your future car shopping preferences in exchange for dealer trade-in matches.

questions.question: What does the guide say the car is worth, and what moved the number?
questions.why: Reviewing the exact deductions for mileage, color, and tire condition helps you understand how the final cash estimate of $19,900 to $22,900 was calculated.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to see exactly how specific details like worn tires or color choice negatively impact the car's overall valuation.

questions.why: The screen shows a loading spinner in the 'Compare Your Values' section, meaning the actual cash offer for the [address] Corvette has not yet been displayed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: If the agent navigates away before the spinner resolves, you lose the specific Kelley Blue Book valuation needed to accurately evaluate the car's price.

questions.question: Should you price the car with only standard equipment to see its baseline value?
questions.why: The NADA Guides table currently shows higher 'Price + Options' values for trade-in and retail, so selecting standard equipment reveals the vehicle's base value before add-ons.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide whether to evaluate the car's price based on its specific options or just its standard baseline features.

questions.question: Does the aggregator cover every site you wanted, or do some need their own search?
questions.why: Seeing the logos for sites like eBay, Craigslist, and Carvana confirms exactly which marketplaces are included in this aggregated search.

questions.question: Which regional search tabs actually contain matching listings, and which ones are empty?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the geographic awareness of exactly which regions have available inventory for your specific car search.

questions.question: Did the external site keep the filters set on the aggregator?
questions.why: Checking that the 87 results for Toyota Siennas in Denver match your original criteria ensures the aggregator successfully transferred your search parameters.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to verify that the aggregator successfully passed your specific search criteria to the external marketplace.

questions.question: Should you cross-check the TrueCar estimate with another source like Edmunds?
questions.why: Relying on a single estimate might not give you the full picture, and seeing options like 'Appraise My Car' on Edmunds provides a chance to verify the vehicle's true market value.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to decide which specific pricing authorities to trust and compare before making a final judgment on the car's value.

questions.question: Are you recording the depreciated used car value or the original new car MSRP?
questions.why: The screen displayed a 'New Car Prices' heading with an MSRP, meaning this number represents the original price rather than the current value of the used car.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose an accurate estimate of the used car's actual market price if the agent mistakenly records the original new car MSRP.

questions.question: Does the value written into the spreadsheet match the figure the pricing site showed for that year?
questions.why: The spreadsheet has a specific cell in the Value column for the 2011 car where the researched price must be recorded.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the assurance that the agent correctly transcribed the exact vehicle price into your tracking document.

questions.question: How far apart are the pricing tools on this car?
questions.why: The text editor displays estimates ranging from $9,600 to over $14,000, requiring you to determine which valuation is the most trustworthy.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to apply your own financial judgment to weigh conflicting price estimates and decide what the car is actually worth.

questions.question: Which pricing guides are being compared?
questions.why: Comparing NADA Guides, Kelley Blue Book, and live Craigslist listings provides a comprehensive view of trade-in, retail, and private market values.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally weigh the nuances between institutional book values and real-world local asking prices.

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the human skepticism needed to question a misleading algorithm and realize the car is actually priced well over its original MSRP.

questions.question: Are even the cheapest listings priced above what the car cost new?
questions.why: The screen showed the lowest priced models starting at $28,100, which is important to note because it reveals whether the used market is still inflated above the original MSRP.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the contextual awareness to realize these used prices are actually inflated above MSRP and the intuition to cross-check another marketplace.

questions.question: Does the current asking price make sense compared to the original MSRP on the window sticker?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to spot unreasonable price gouging by cross-referencing the current listing price with the original manufacturer documents.

questions.question: Are there listings on the price-by-year graph priced well below the others for their year?
questions.why: The screen displays a scatter plot of Jeeps in Seattle by asking price and model year, which helps identify pricing trends and outliers for specific models.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to visually spot market trends or identify uniquely priced outlier vehicles that might represent a great deal.

questions.question: At which year do prices on the graph stop dropping steeply?
questions.why: Visually analyzing the plotted data points helps identify the specific model years where the car stops rapidly losing value.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to apply your own judgment to visual market trends to find your ideal balance of age and price.

questions.question: Do these prices include shipping, and how much does it add?
questions.why: The search results showed 17 matches with base prices ranging from $31,998 to $37,998, plus significant shipping fees up to $1,899 that must be factored into the total cost.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally weigh the trade-offs between a cheaper car with a higher shipping fee versus a more expensive local option.

questions.question: What's a fair price to offer, given what the guides say?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally weigh the different appraisal values to decide on a negotiation target you feel comfortable with.

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to visually verify crucial details in the photos, such as physical trim badges and warranty stickers, which might differ from or supplement the text description.

videocall.task: set up or join a video call (Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams): either create/schedule a meeting and invite someone, or join with a link or code; work through the audio/video device prompts and arrive in the live meeting; complete when the in-meeting screen with the user's own audio/video controls is shown. Surface pinned: the meeting product's own host/join flow — not webinar spectating, not call-quality reviews, not presentations ABOUT video calling.

tree.label: Join a video call
tree.note: 1 where the session is not already inside the product - most keepers start signed in; 1.6 on the four Zoom sign-ups. then either the host route or the guest route. host: 2 for a meeting now or a link for later, or 3 for a scheduled one, then 4 to get the joining information out - 4 can also run from inside the meeting after 5. guest: 5.1 to 5.7 to find the way in. both routes run 5.8 where the product asks about opening the app, then 5.10 and 5.11; a guest may stop in 5.12. 6 on the host side once a guest asks to join. 7 and 8 in any order while the meeting runs - every keeper that reaches 5.11 tours them. 9 to leave, and 9.4 loops back to 5.

IRZc runs 3.1 to 3.12 and ends on Discard with nothing saved.

questions.question: How often should this meeting repeat, and on which days?
questions.why: The custom recurrence dialog requires selecting a frequency interval and toggling the exact days of the week the meeting will take place.

questions.question: When should this recurring meeting series end?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to align the meeting's lifespan perfectly with your real-world schedule or project duration.

children.note: Zoom only - Meet has no such section and Teams is never scheduled in the corpus. 3.7.1 then 3.7.2 then 3.7.3, in the order the form lists them; 3.7.4 is read and left off in every keeper. the corpus keeps the generated ID and the generated passcode every time and turns the waiting room on where it is off.

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means the agent decides the method of distributing the meeting invitation to your intended participants.

questions.why: The browser prompt asks for permission to open the meeting in the Teams application, which determines whether the call takes place in the dedicated app or the web browser.

questions.why: The removal confirmation dialog includes checkboxes to fill out an abuse report or block the person from rejoining the call.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the discretion to decide whether a participant should just be temporarily removed for technical reasons or permanently blocked for inappropriate behavior.

children.label: Use the call controls
children.note: any order and any subset - this is the tour every keeper runs after 5.11. 7.1 and 7.2 nearly always; 7.3 and 7.5 where the narrator opens the menus; 7.6 on most; 7.7 and 7.4 where offered; 7.8 only on the Teams participant path; 7.9 once.

questions.question: After the mute, does the participant list actually show that person as muted, or is their audio still live?
questions.why: The screen shows the mute dialog opening, but after a cut, the participant list still displays an active audio icon instead of a muted one.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent would be confused by the inconsistent state and fail to learn how to properly complete the action.

questions.question: After the toggle, do the mic and camera buttons show the state you asked for?
questions.why: The screen displays toggle buttons for the camera and microphone, allowing you to control your privacy and background noise.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means the agent might leave your devices active by default, potentially broadcasting your private environment or background noise before you are ready.

questions.question: Do you want live captions on?
questions.why: The screen provides a 'Turn on captions' button that displays real-time text of the spoken conversation.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to decide if they need real-time visual text support to follow the meeting.

questions.question: How do you want to arrange the video feeds on your screen?
questions.why: The menu provides multiple layout options like 'Gallery at top' and 'Together mode' to customize how you view the other participants.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose the ability to choose a visual layout that best suits your personal viewing preferences for the meeting.

questions.question: Do you want to hide everyone's video and show only the shared content?
questions.why: Selecting 'Focus on content' from the 'More actions' menu removes the video gallery so the presentation can be viewed without visual distractions.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to customize your personal viewing layout to match your own focus preferences during the meeting.

questions.question: Do you want to pop out the shared content into a separate window?
questions.why: The top menu bar includes a 'Pop out' button that allows you to separate the presentation from the main meeting window to better manage your screen space.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose the ability to customize your personal screen layout and window arrangement during the live meeting.

questions.question: Do you want to pin your own share or camera to see what others see?
questions.why: Clicking the 'Presentation (You)' or 'You' thumbnails lets you enlarge your own feeds to confirm exactly what is being broadcast to the meeting.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the personal peace of mind that comes from visually confirming your camera and screen share look correct to others.

questions.question: What video resolution do you want to set for sending and receiving?
questions.why: The video settings offer high definition (720p) or standard definition (360p) options, allowing you to balance video quality against your available internet bandwidth.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means the agent might select a high resolution that causes lag on a poor connection, or default to a lower quality when you actually have the bandwidth for high definition.

questions.question: Does the call show a connection or quality warning?
questions.why: The Call health panel displays real-time technical metrics like the sent frame rate and latency to help you verify the quality of your connection.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally monitor the real-time technical quality of your connection and diagnose potential network or hardware issues.

questions.question: What message, emoji, or GIF should I send in the meeting chat?
questions.why: The screen shows the meeting chat pane with text input, emoji menus, and GIF search options for interacting with other participants.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to personally express their tone and spontaneous reactions using specific text, emojis, or GIFs.

questions.question: Which reaction do you want to put on the message?
questions.why: The screen shows a hover menu with multiple reaction icons like Heart and Laugh over the chat messages.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to express their personal emotional response to specific messages in the chat.

questions.question: Do you want to raise your hand or send a reaction?
questions.why: The Reactions menu displays emojis and a 'Raise hand' option that trigger visual feedback on your video feed to communicate silently with other participants.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally time your hand raise or select the most appropriate emotional reaction for the ongoing conversation.

questions.question: Do you want to open the queue for the raised hand?
questions.why: The screen displays a popup notification that a participant has raised their hand, offering a choice to either open the queue or dismiss the prompt.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide whether to immediately acknowledge a participant's question or wait until a better time in the meeting.

questions.question: Do you want to take control of the shared presentation?
questions.why: The screen shows a shared presentation with a 'Take control' button and slide navigation controls.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent taking control without permission could disrupt the current presenter and the flow of the meeting.

questions.question: Should I open the slide grid so you can move through the slides on your own?
questions.why: The screen displays a grid view button that opens thumbnails of the slides, allowing you to jump to a specific slide on your end only.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to privately browse and review specific presentation slides at your own pace during the live meeting.

questions.question: Do you want to open the meeting notes panel?
questions.why: The in-call menu includes a 'Meeting notes' option to start capturing text notes directly within the meeting interface.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose the ability to personally format and record the initial discussion points for the team.

children.label: Present and record
children.note: 8.1 on most keepers - and half of them open the share dialog and cancel. 8.2 where a whiteboard is demonstrated - three products and three kinds of board. 8.3 where recording is shown; on Meet's free tier 8.3.1 finds nothing and 8.3.2 goes outside the product. any order, while the meeting runs.

children.label: Share the screen
children.note: 8.1.1 first - the choice is made in that dialog and the tutorials read all three options. 8.1.2 where a tab or window is picked and sound matters. 8.1.3 on Teams only. then 8.1.4, or Cancel - ipyP and wGXI and 0Qvm and IRZc never share. 8.1.5 on A2Fa and inside 4Qyi's floating bar. 8.1.6 closes it, from the product or from the browser's banner.

questions.question: Do you want to share the whole screen, a window, or a tab?
questions.why: The menu provides distinct sharing modes for your entire screen, a specific window, or a Chrome tab that is explicitly optimized for video and animation.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might not understand the specific media format or privacy requirements of your content to choose the most appropriate and secure sharing mode.

questions.question: Where should your video sit on the share, and how big?
questions.why: The 'Edit your view' window provides a size slider and position icons so you can ensure your video feed doesn't block important shared content.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally fine-tune the exact placement and scale of your video feed over your presentation.

questions.question: Are you ready to stop sharing your screen with the meeting participants?
questions.why: The presenter toolbar at the top of the screen displays a 'Stop presenting' icon, indicating that your screen is currently visible to everyone in the call.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide exactly when to end the broadcast, which could risk exposing private information if the agent leaves the screen share active.

children.label: Use a whiteboard
children.note: 8.2.1 opens one - Jamboard through Activities or the More menu on Meet, the Whiteboard tile in Zoom's share dialog, Miro as an add-on. 8.2.2 where the narrator draws. 8.2.3 on Meet only - the board is a separate tab or app and has to be presented back into the call, or started as a collaboration on Miro. Zoom's board is the share.

questions.question: Do you want to open a shared whiteboard?
questions.why: Clicking the Activities icon reveals a 'Whiteboarding' option to collaboratively brainstorm and sketch ideas with other participants.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to spontaneously initiate a shared visual workspace for brainstorming during the meeting.

questions.question: Which activity or add-on do you want to open?
questions.why: The screen presented built-in activities like breakout rooms and polls alongside third-party add-ons like Miro, requiring a choice of which collaboration tool to open.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose the ability to decide which specific collaboration tool or add-on best fits the current flow of the meeting.

questions.question: Do you want everyone to see the board now?
questions.why: A blue pop-up offers a 'Start collaboration' button because the board is not automatically visible to the other people in the meeting.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the choice of exactly when to reveal the collaborative workspace to your attendees.

questions.question: Should you accept the invitation to join the Miro collaboration board?
questions.why: The screen displays a prompt from Charlies Lessons inviting you to move the call to a Miro whiteboard in a new tab.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose the ability to decide whether to participate in the external whiteboard activity or remain solely in the main meeting interface.

children.label: Record the meeting
children.note: 8.3.1 first - and what it finds decides the rest: local or cloud on Zoom, an admin gate on G Suite, nothing on free Meet. 8.3.2 only in 0Qvm, outside the product. then 8.3.3, and 8.3.4 after the meeting ends where the tutorial follows the file.

questions.question: Do you want to let this recording extension read and change your data on every website?
questions.why: The browser popup explicitly warns that installing this extension gives it broad access to read and change your data across all websites.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to evaluate the privacy and security risks of giving a third-party extension broad access to your browsing data.

questions.question: Do you want to start recording the meeting?
questions.why: The 'More actions' menu displays the 'Start recording' option, allowing you to capture the live meeting for future reference.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide whether the meeting's content is appropriate or necessary to record.

questions.question: Do you want to stop recording the meeting?
questions.why: The system displays a confirmation dialog asking if you are sure you want to stop the active recording.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide exactly when the conversation should go off the official record.

questions.question: Did the recording link actually appear in the meeting chat as the banner promised?
questions.why: Checking the chat thread confirms that the system fulfilled the banner's promise to deliver the stopped recording.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the immediate reassurance of personally confirming that the meeting recording was successfully generated and saved.

questions.question: Do you want the recording downloaded, or just its link saved?
questions.why: The tl;dv recording page displays the captured video, transcript, and icons to download or copy the link, requiring a choice on how to distribute the file.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose the ability to personally decide who receives the recording link or whether the file is downloaded for your own secure records.

children.label: Leave or end the meeting
children.note: 9.1 on every host that ends on camera - End meeting for all every time in the corpus. 9.2 where the product confirms - Zoom asks and Meet does not. 9.3 on Meet after any leave. 9.4 loops back to 5 - d8L2 from the left-screen and 3Og- and wGXI by starting over.

questions.question: Do you want to leave the meeting now?
questions.why: The meeting control bar features a prominent red 'Leave' button with a phone icon that immediately disconnects you from the live session.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the ability to decide exactly when to conclude your presence and exit the conversation.

questions.question: Do you want to rate the call quality, or just return to the home screen?
questions.why: The post-meeting screen displays a star rating prompt for audio and video quality alongside the option to return to the home screen.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to provide feedback on their specific call experience to the platform.

questions.question: Do you want to rejoin after landing on the 'left the meeting' screen?
questions.why: The screen displays options to rejoin, return to the home screen, or submit feedback, requiring a choice to recover from the interruption.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to decide whether to immediately rejoin the meeting or abandon the attempt after being disconnected.
